In emerging countries, mortality has been growing steadily. A helmet detection technology that identifies drivers without helmets is needed to safeguard the public. We employ a real-time 3202 dataset for this approach. We gather wearing helmet 1911 and no helmet 1291 data and utilize algorithms like VGG16, Resnet50, MobileNet v.02, Inception V3, EfficientNet, and CNN. The EfficientNet achieved 98% accuracy. Each person's comparison statement techniques are in the implementation section. To construct the optimum model for the conditions, this inquiry uses model validation approaches.

articleTitle: An Expert System for Facial Micro-Expressions Based Lie Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: For the purpose of assisting authorities like the police and attorneys in court, lie detection in humans is an important topic of research. Although there has been a lot of research in this area, the polygraph remains the most often utilized method. The development of technology has made it possible to record minute facial expressions and nonverbal clues that are difficult to see with the unaided eye. In this study, we seek to identify specific facial cues that could aid in the development of a reliable and effective lie-detection project. To choose the most effective strategy, we will evaluate our facial expression and micro-expression performance metrics. The results are Based on the Duchenne smile and the connection between lying and an increase in blink rate. This paper explores the applications of OpenCV to lie detection.

articleTitle: Deep learning based Wireless Capsule Endoscopy for Small Intestinal Lesions Detection and personalized treatment pathways
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) revolutionizes disease diagnosis by analyzing medical data and improving clinical tasks. This paper proposes an integrated approach that combines deep learning algorithms with Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) for enhanced small intestinal lesion detection. Our methodology integrates WCE images, electronic health records (EHR), and genomic data using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for feature extraction. By analyzing these data sources, we aim to uncover correlations between clinical factors, genetic markers, and small intestinal lesions. This approach enables customized treatment plans based on individual patient characteristics and genetic profiles, contributing to improved patient outcomes in gastroenterology. Our study highlights the importance of incorporating AI technologies in medical practice, promoting precision medicine and enhancing patient care. The integration of deep learning with WCE offers a promising avenue for personalized treatment strategies, optimizing the management of small intestinal lesions.

articleTitle: Epidemic Modeling using Hybrid of Time-varying SIRD, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Epidemiological models are best suitable to model an epidemic if the spread pattern is stationary. To deal with non-stationary patterns and multiple waves of an epidemic, we develop a hybrid model encompassing epidemic modeling, particle swarm optimization, and deep learning. The model mainly caters to three objectives for better prediction: 1. Periodic estimation of the model parameters. 2. Incorporating impact of all the aspects using data fitting and parameter optimization 3. Deep learning based prediction of the model parameters. In our model, we use a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Dead (SIRD) epidemic modeling, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for model parameter optimization, and stacked-LSTM for forecasting the model parameters. Initial or one time estimation of model parameters is not able to model multiple waves of an epidemic. So, we estimate the model parameters periodically (weekly). We use PSO to identify the optimum values of the model parameters. We next train the stacked-LSTM on the optimized parameters, and perform forecasting of the model parameters for upcoming four weeks. Further, we fed the LSTM forecasted parameters into the SIRD model to forecast the number of COVID-19 cases. We evaluate the model for highly affected three countries namely; the USA, India, and the UK. The proposed hybrid model is able to deal with multiple waves, and has outperformed existing methods on all the three datasets.

articleTitle: Streamlining Email Workflow: Empowering Users with Voice Recognition Technology and Website-Email Autometa Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s business-oriented society, email is used to send all official communications. Many institutions, colleges, and IT industries, in addition to the commercial sector, provide official information via email. Manually sending emails to everyone is an extremely time-consuming task. Therefore, a website that uses speech-to-text recognition to send emails and system talks to user about tasks done. The Email Autometa Solutions website is a Streamlit-based web app that allows users to automate email sending using voice commands. The website integrates voice recognition, email composition, and email sending functionalities to provide a streamlined and user-friendly experience. Users can input the email subject and message by speaking, and even attach files if needed. The website leverages libraries such as pyttsx3 for text-to-speech conversion and speech_recognition for speech-to-text conversion. Once the email is composed, it is sent via SMTP using the Gmail server. The website provides audio feedback to notify users about the success or failure of the email sending process. With its intuitive interface and voice-based input, the Email Autometa Solutions website simplifies and accelerates the email sending workflow.

articleTitle: Predicting Student Failure using Peer-based Evaluation and Ratings
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Detecting student performance in programming is essential for educators to refine their teaching methodologies and for students to gain insight into their strengths and areas needing improvement. This research paper focuses on the accurate identification of students who may struggle or require additional support in understanding the Java programming language. Data was collected through an online questionnaire and an offline exam based on Java, involving 111 Master of Computer Applications (MCA) students. The exam incorporated peer-based evaluation, where students’ answer sheets were assessed by peers from the same class. A total of 29 attributes, including peer evaluation ratings and student behavior survey attributes, were considered for analysis. To identify students requiring additional assistance, five machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Decision Tree, were employed. By leveraging various features and patterns within the student data, these algorithms effectively determined which students may need extra support in their Java programming skills. Random Forest yielded the highest overall accuracy of 96.43%. The primary goal of this study is to enable faculty members to concentrate their efforts on supporting and improving the knowledge of students who are at higher risk of failing or require further focus on Java programming. The findings from this research will aid in providing targeted assistance to the identified students, thereby enhancing their understanding and performance in Java programming. The successful implementation of machine learning algorithms for detecting students in need of support contributes to the continuous improvement of student learning outcomes and teaching methodologies.

articleTitle: Secure Automated Inventory Management system using Abstracted System Design Microservice Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Managing inventory has forever been a difficult problem for e-commerce sellers. Even today manual labor is used for the major part of the job. Without much automation in this industry growth has been stagnant because of the same reason.The proposed system works on a microservice-based architecture that enables automated inventory management with the help of a social-media messaging bot in an abstract manner. The bot comprises an integrated hybrid recommender system at the customer’s end for better recommendations based on image and textual data. The entire system is deployed on the cloud following a serverless architecture for resilient service. The proposed solution plays a key role in taking research forward in the direction of micro-service-based system design involving real-world data. The results of the experiment prove to be beneficial for customers and retailers since they are now connected using the micro-service.

articleTitle: Eye Gaze Correction System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The process of gaze correction involves manipulating the eye region of an individual in order to redirect their gaze towards the camera. This method, which is a particular kind of image resynthesis, may be used to take pictures where the subject appears to be looking straight at the camera, among many other practical uses. Using an inpainting model, we present a novel method for accomplishing gaze correction in this research. With our method, we train a face-to-face learning model on photos, then manually fill in the blanks where the eyes should be. A benefit of our approach is that it does not necessitate labelled training data that provides information about the exact location of the head and the orientation of the eyes. As a result, we had a rather easy time amassing the training data we needed. To retain the eye area identification information in the original input, we present a self-guided pretrained model that can learn angle-invariant properties. Our tests show that, when applied to a dataset gathered from multiple websites, our approach produces incredibly convincing gaze-corrected results. In our study, we go into detail about this dataset.

articleTitle: FERLP: Facial Emotion Recognition Based on Landmark Points using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the field of emotion processing, it can be challenging to determine how to identify a person's state of mind from their realistic expressions of emotion when working in an environment with several dimensions. There have been various investigations and projects done to develop strategies for generating accurate predictions; nevertheless, very little has been done to put the distinctive characteristics of the face of a person to use when interpreting and reacting to the emotional expressions of other people. An emotional picture retrieval approach is proposed for use in multimodal emotion detection in this body of work. This tactic is predicated on the observations that facial characteristics are present at all times and that the human face possesses regional redundancy that is independent of facial characteristics. Our approach makes use of landmark points to strip away any superfluous information on facial expressions, allowing us to zero in on the most appealing examples from each individual frame. If we make use of the landmarks, it's possible that we'll be able to forecast facial expressions with a greater degree of accuracy. This is especially important for long-term emotion prediction because it helps us restore time and space representations when an emotional face is introduced. The preliminary findings derived from a standard dataset indicate that the suggested strategy outperforms its rivals with regard to the accuracy of the predictions it generates.

articleTitle: Solar Irradiance Forecasting Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of solar irradiance is crucial for minimizing uncertainty of the solar energy output from PV plants, as solar irradiance can be utilized to determine the solar energy produced. The proposed models use the historical solar irradiance data along with 8 features namely temperature, dew, humidity, wind gust, wind speed, cloud cover, pressure, and visibility. The primary objective is to create a model that forecasts solar irradiance accurately. LSTM, GRU, SVR, and BiLSTM models are used and they are trained and tested on a dataset of 7 months with the frequency of one hour collected from a site in Tamil Nadu. By calculating the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), the performance of the models are evaluated. The LSTM model has performed better than other models and gave better accuracy in terms of RMSE and MAE.

articleTitle: Generation of Royalty-Free Images with NLP-Based Text Encoding and Generative adversarial networks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces the AttnGAN, an Attentional Generative Adversarial Network that facilitates detailed text-to-image generation through multi-stage refinement driven by attention. The AttnGAN employs a unique attentional generative network that generates images with precise details in different subregions by focusing on relevant words in the textual description. The detailed image-text similarity loss is calculated using a deep cognitive multimodal resemblance model to further improve the training of the generator. Furthermore, we have evaluated the proposed AttnGAN on two widely used datasets, namely CUB and COCO. The investigational outcomes indicate that our model can accurately synthesis high-quality images on the CUB dataset. However, the performance of our model is not as satisfactory on the COCO dataset, which poses a more challenging text-to-image generation task because of the complex and diverse scenes in the dataset. Nonetheless, our proposed attention mechanisms have demonstrated their effectiveness, especially for generating fine-grained details in the images.

articleTitle: A comprehensive investigation into the use of machine learning to forecast ovarian cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ovarian cancer, a deadly disease, affects women worldwide. Early detection improves treatment and survival. This research investigates ovarian cancer prediction using machine learning, a potential technology. Ovarian cancer's history, symptoms, and current diagnosis are covered. Early detection and machine learning's potential to improve diagnosis and therapy are highlighted. Machine learning ovarian cancer prediction research is summarised next. Discussions include logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines. We compare method accuracy and discuss their pros and cons. The study suggests machine learning algorithms could predict ovarian cancer. Model accuracy and AUC values showed strong forecast performance. These findings can improve clinical early diagnosis and treatment outcomes, the scientists say. The paper concludes with the study's drawbacks, including the need for larger datasets and more diverse patient populations. The authors advise using deep learning and genomes and proteomics data to advance the area.

articleTitle: ChatGPT, a powerful language model and its potential uses in bioinformatics
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This review investigates the future potential of ChatGPT, a transformer-based large language model (LLM), in bioinformatics applications such as text mining, protein sequence analysis, drug development, and clinical decision-making. Several research has demonstrated the success of ChatGPT in various domains, and its adaptability and versatility make it a valuable tool in the bioinformatics toolbox. ChatGPT's ability to learn and adapt to new data and tasks sets it apart from existing approaches, and its use has the potential to revolutionize how researchers analyze and interpret biological data. ChatGPT, has major applications in scientific literature review and text mining. Research has shown that pre-training GPT like models with biological text has improved the accuracy and reliability of such models when dealing with biological data. Additionally, ChatGPT shows a lot of promise in bioinformatics and has the potential to help a lot of people, due to its ubiquitousness and ease of handling. Major limitations and drawbacks of using ChatGPT involve its inability to handle complex biological data such as genomic data and also a large amount of training data is required to generate accurate results. But with the advancing technologies and development on newer advanced GPT models, can easily provide potential solutions to these limitations.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection Using Semantic Analysis and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the era of online information dissemination, the challenge of fake news and disinformation has become increasingly severe, making reliable detection crucial for maintaining the integrity of information ecosystems. Using semantic analysis and several forms of machine learning, the authors of this research study provide an innovative method for identifying instances of false news. To describe the contextual semantics of textual data more precisely, we use Word Embeddings and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. From multiple internet sources, we gathered a dataset of real and false news stories, which we then preprocessed using tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, and sequence padding. To capture the semantic links between words and phrases, we employed the Global Vectors for Word Representation (GloVe) to convert each word into a dense vector representation. This was used to feed a stacked LSTM model, a kind of RNN that can recognise long-distance relationships in text data. Our suggested approach beat conventional models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and LSTM without Word Embeddings during rigorous testing. Our method achieved an accuracy of 0.92, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining LSTM networks with Word Embeddings for fake news detection. Despite these promising results, challenges related to language generalization, sensitivity to word embedding quality, and inclusion of additional sources of information remain. Our research signifies a key contribution to the ongoing fight against fake news and disinformation, providing an effective approach to detect fake news with potential for further enhancement and application in real-world scenarios. Future work could focus on fine-tuning the model for different languages and domains, improving word embeddings, and integrating additional information sources to further improve fake news detection.

articleTitle: A Prairie Dog Optimized Neural Network-Based Hybrid DC-AC Microgrid Energy Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this study, we present a Prairie dog optimization to switch energy feeding in AC-DC hybrid distribution networks using artificial neural networks. It is suggested to put in place an energy management system that accounts for load demand, distributed generation, and battery charge status. An artificial neural network was trained using the profile data to analyze the characteristics of charging and discharging an energy storage device under different distribution-network power conditions. The error rate was maintained far below 10%, which was another advantage. The proposed energy management system makes use of a neural network trained to perform as ideally as possible with the help of an optimizer inspired by prairie dogs and given the catchy name "Prairie dog optimization. Using information about the distributed generator's output, the utility grid's output, and a direct-axis reference current, Prairie dog optimization refines the neural network's bias and weights to create the most effective energy management system possible. Small-scale hybrid AC/DC microgrids have been carried out and tested in order to mimic and assess the proposed energy management system. In comparison to other systems in the literature, the Prairie dog optimization optimizer enhanced neural network energy management system has been shown to be the most effective option, with an efficiency of 99.55 percent.

articleTitle: Real-Time Web Application to Classify Diabetic Foot Ulcer
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers are one of the major complications of type 2 diabetes and can result in gangrene and amputation if left untreated. Early detection and treatment are essential for reducing the risk of amputation. Imaging, such as digital photography or imaging scans, can be a valuable tool in detecting and monitoring diabetic foot ulcers, documenting their size and location, identifying underlying issues, and evaluating treatment effectiveness. This paper utilises a two-dimensional image as its input and applies an ensemble of neural networks to analyse the images. The system is capable of performing image classification into four distinct states, infection, ischaemia, both, and none.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Analysis of 3.5 GHz Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study focuses on designing and analyzing a microstrip patch antenna that operates at 3.5 GHz, specifically for wireless communication systems. Rogers RT5880 (lossy) has a dielectric permittivity of 2.2 and a loss tangent of 0.0009 and has been used as a substrate material to design the antenna. Besides, CST Studio software has been used to create and simulate the antenna. There is a lot of antenna design software; special software is CST, HFSS, MATLAB, FEKO, ADS, and others. Among them, CST software is the most widely used antenna design, and the results are comparatively better than other software. The results obtained from the designed simulation show that return loss, VSWR, gain, directivity, bandwidth, and efficiency are -28.29 dB, 1.0801, 5.437 dBi, 6.442dBi, and 111.7 MHz, respectively. The main focus of said research is to reduce return loss and VSWR. That is to develop a standard VSWR whose value is close to 1 and less than 2. Besides, increasing the gain and directivity of the antenna and improving the efficiency. Efficiency accounted for 84.39% of the total. The design could be used in future wireless LANs applications because of their good impedance matching, gain, return loss, VSWR, Bandwidth and accuracy.

articleTitle: Software Defect Prediction Model Using AdaBoost based Random Forest Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Software testing is a crucial step in the development procedure. Typically, the defects or errors caused by developers are often dealt with a while later in software development, leading to an increased effect or influence of these flaws. In order to stop this from happening, issues must be identified early in the software development process allowing for the effective use of testing resources. As part of the defect prediction process, software modules are categorized as either defect-prone or non-defect-prone. To automate and enhance the prediction of defective software modules a key criterion for the analysis, numerous methods have been anticipated. In this paper, we create a combined model that assesses the presence of defects in a software module. The proposed work has been based on pre-processing, feature dimensionality reduction and classification. The model is tested through a publicly available NASA dataset. We have applied principal component analysis (PCA) for feature dimensionality reduction, which reduces the dimension of the feature vector. During the prediction task, the boosting technique called AdaBoost has been applied to a random forest named ABRF to determine the prediction rate. Several performance metrics which include accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score and MCC are measured to validate the planned model. The results of the PCA+ABRF method show that the model has an average accuracy of 0.9862 for the KC2 dataset. From the experimental results, it has been observed that the proposed model provides better defect prediction accuracy as compared to other existing models.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphone Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In day-to-day existence, people act on many tasks. It is vital to record and analyze the daily presence of individual people. Hence it could assist with relieving a few medical conditions and different issues. Human Activity Recognizing is a key component of research topics in computer vision for different sectors like security monitoring, healthcare and human-computer association, and sports. Nowadays, the smartphone has become popular and helpful for people. Because smartphone has many various and effective sensors, in this paper, we have used smartphone sensors: an accelerometer and gyroscope to detect human activity. In our research, we collected 30 study participants labeled datasets between ages nine-teen to four-ty-eight (19-48) years who have executed actions such as activities of daily life including sitting, walking, standing, walking up or down stairs, and lying down while using a smartphone equipped with such sensors. The objective is to do each of the six activities in the correct order. Two sets of the recorded dataset were randomly chosen, with 70% of participants 30% chosen to produce test data, and the remaining 70% to produce training data. The results were gained along with compared by supervised classification algorithms such as Random Forest, decision trees, KNN method, Support vector machines, and Logistic Regression. By comparing those algorithms, we gained the best results accuracy from Logistic Regression which is 96.21%.

articleTitle: Network Analysis of Research Base Papers: Metrics and Potential use
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper describes a common challenge faced by researchers who struggle to find good references for their current domain of study due to the exponential increase in research papers being published daily. The proposed solution involves using deep learning techniques with the BERT Model to obtain a summary of the published paper and its citation papers. Science mapping approaches are then applied to ascertain the similarity between the reference papers and the original paper and rank the citations based on their similarity. Various bibliometric analyses such as citation analysis, co-citation analysis, bibliometric coupling, and network metrics are used to further rank the citations and identify unique citations with citation count. Additionally, author suggestions are provided. The end goal is to develop a visualization tool in the form of a dashboard to help researchers focus on relevant papers.

articleTitle: IBit a Novel Representation for Multidimensional Information Universal Database
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: According to modern physics theories, all of the universe's materials, energy, particles, and dimensions are interconnected information in a multidimensional network that can be expressed as mere numbers and defined under the information theory. The information is organized in a multidimensional structure whose construction unit is suggested in this paper to be ibit which represents an abstract number instead of a classical bit. This number represents the building unit of the information system (universal database) so the selection of the appropriate ibit will help to organize this multidimensional structure and can reduce the number of the universal database dimensions. Hence, using a binary system will result in a very complex system, whereas using a decimal or hexadecimal order reduces the number of dimensions and clarifies the interconnectedness of information. Similarly, using fractional complex rather than integer will lead to additional arrangement and clarification of the multidimensional structure in the same format. This paper will be a new and distinctive first step toward representing arithmetic numbers in an informational format interconnected in the form of information with a systematic and multidimensional structure. This step is critical for activating and generalizing information theory for everything, and the research will propose a distinctive definition of dimensions that is compatible with the theory of information as well as reveal the most significant weaknesses in today's enumeration systems through analysis and suggest the best ways to expand them in the future, thus expanding the horizon of technology and engineering to areas that may be revolutionary.

articleTitle: ASDEXPLAINER : An Interpretable Graph Neural Network Framework for Brain Network Based Autism Spectrum Disorder Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Understanding the predictions made by GNN models can lead to significant breakthroughs in trusting these models to be used for safety critical healthcare applications. GNNs are excellent at modeling non euclidean data such as graphs, but many scientists refrain from using them because of their blackbox nature. This is due to the ambiguity that exists regarding the background mechanisms that lead to predictions. Human brain can be effectively modeled as a graph, which is formally known as the brain network which is in turn used for studying interactions between various brain regions when it is affected by some disorder. Our work aims to conduct a comparative analysis among the explanations generated by various modified GNN explainability models for a pre-trained GNN model over Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) fMRI dataset. It mainly comprises 2 phases. The first being training a GNN model tailor-made for brain networks which highlights salient ROIs by using functional and structural information from fMRI. Secondly, the explanation generator that uses GNN explainability methods is modified specifically to suit brain network data to generate explanations about the predictions by discovering neurological biomarkers. We evaluate the performance of the explanation generator by employing various evaluation metrics. The obtained results show great correspondence with the ground truth explanations regarding the brain regions that get affected by autism.

articleTitle: Towards Smart Agriculture: Automated Detection and Diagnosis of Bean Leaf Diseases Using ResNext50 Model
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Bean leaf halo blight is a widespread plant disease that causes large output losses by affecting the leaves of bean plants. This disease is known as bean leaf halo blight. To develop successful methods for illness management, it is essential to determine the seriousness levels of this disease in a precise and timely manner. The proposed research study present a multi-classification framework that makes use of the ResNeXt50 model to categorize bean leaf halo blight according to one of five distinct seriousness levels. The authors want to achieve the goal of developing a dependable and effective system by utilizing the capabilities of deep learning (DL) and transfer learning (TL). This will allow us to provide farmers with assistance in making well-informed decisions on disease management methods. To make the model more robust, we amped up the data by collecting and processing a collection of bean leaf pictures and by using data augmentation strategies. After being trained and tested, the ResNeXt50 model was found to have an accuracy level of 96.37% overall. Following the investigation of performance parameters for each layer, a confusion matrix was developed to evaluate the classification results produced by the model. In addition, the ResNeXt50 model was judged to be superior to other cutting-edge models under its ability to effectively categorize bean leaf halo blight. This was demonstrated by a comparison with other models. The framework that has been developed has the potential to greatly improve disease control practices, contribute to the enhancement of crop yields, and ensure that agriculture remains sustainable. Future research may concentrate on improving the model and evaluating its performance in real-world settings; this will contribute to the practical implementation of the suggested system.

articleTitle: Revamping Machining Operator Allowances through Standard Time Estimation using MOST Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Time and motion study plays a crucial role in optimizing plant efficiency by identifying and eliminating non-value-added activities that can hinder productivity. Excessive work content resulting from such activities can lead to increased production time and costs. Addressing these issues requires the elimination of operator idle time and the synchronization of work content to reduce effort and enhance productivity. The Maynard Operation Sequence Technique (MOST) is a highly effective work measurement technique that enables quick, accurate, and effortless measurement of various types of work, spanning manufacturing, engineering, and administrative service activities. In this paper, we propose the application of the MOST technique to provide allowances for proper sculptured surface machining. The technique involves an alignment process that fulfills a user-defined set of criteria for specific operations, ensuring the provision of machining allowances. By determining process-oriented allowances, relevant and acceptable time standards can be established within the industry. The utilization of the MOST technique in time and motion study has demonstrated significant potential for improving plant efficiency through the identification of non-value-added activities, reduction of idle time, and synchronization of work content among operators. This research contributes to enhancing industrial productivity and offers insights into the effective utilization of the MOST technique in diverse operational contexts.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Enhancing Data Aggregation Security in the Internet of Medical Things
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this study, we focus on addressing the security and privacy challenges associated with the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and associated data. IoMT involves the transmission of large volumes of real-time medical data from various small devices. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel approach that combines the Lightweight Encryption Algorithm (LEA) with the Paillier encryption approach. This combination is aimed at improving energy consumption, encryption time, and memory usage. By employing LEA encryption, our approach ensures both confidentiality and data integrity during the transmission of medical data. Additionally, the Paillier encryption technique is leveraged to preserve privacy and facilitate secure data aggregation. Through extensive security analysis and experimental evaluations, we have found that our proposed method achieves average encryption and decryption speeds that are 30% faster and 8% less energy consumption compared to the ECC-AES and ElGamal algorithms.

articleTitle: An Interactive Interview Bot for Human Resource Interviewing
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: It has been difficult for recruiters from various organizations to inform all of their candidates about the interview procedure, which makes holding interviews a bother. Additionally, engaging with a big number of applicants and carrying out additional screening tasks add to the recruitment issues when there are several applicants. A human interviewer’s bias or weariness throughout the interview process could have an impact on the overall selection procedure. The interview process is typically used to screen applicants for open positions. This procedure differs from business to business. However, the technical interview and the human resource interview continue to be the two principal approaches. The conventional interviewing process is labor- and resource-intensive. By utilizing a chatbot in place of a human interviewer, we can automate this procedure. The interview process will be simplified using an interactive interview bot. It’s a robot that can interview candidates and assess their communication abilities, facial expressions, and other traits. The majority of companies rely on their staff to communicate, which could lead to diminished consequences for the business. As a result of its capabilities, Interview Bot significantly accelerates the entire interviewing procedure, streamlining the process and saving valuable time for both recruiters and candidates. With its advanced features and automated functionalities, Interview Bot expedites the overall workflow, making it more efficient and productive.

articleTitle: Efficient mmWave Beam Selection using ViTs and GVEC: GPS-based Virtual Environment Capture
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Millimeter waves (mmWaves) providing higher bandwidth is used by 5G network technology to achieve higher network capacity and faster data transfer. However, the process of beam sweeping across multiple antenna arrays can be time-consuming and inefficient. Machine learning (ML) models can address this issue by predicting the optimal beam pair based on data from on-vehicle light detection and ranging (LIDAR) and global positioning system (GPS) sensors. This paper proposes a new vision transformer (ViT) ML model for beam selection using GPS and LIDAR data. GPS-based virtual environment capture (GVEC) has been introduced to overcome to overcome noise in the LIDAR data caused by adverse weather conditions. The proposed solution demonstrates improved performance compared to previous approaches when tested on noisy LIDAR data, achieving a 92% accuracy in searching among the top 10 beams.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Road Damage Using Deep Learning Approach with Smartphone Images
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In cities, road surface monitoring is mostly done by hand which is a time-consuming and labour-intensive procedure. One of the most critical responsibilities is infrastructure maintenance work for traffic safety. To keep the road network safe, it must be assessed on a regular basis to identify potential threats and risks. We work on detecting and classifying road damage using deep learning approach in this research, which is a low-cost intelligence system. The goal of this work is to investigate the detection and categorization of road damage from road surface photographs using deep learning concept. This study used different transfer learning algorithms to categorize road damage in order to determine which algorithm performed better at detecting and classifying road damage. We divide damages into four groups: potholes, cracks, and revealing and rutting. For this research, we used a smartphone camera to collect data from the streets of Dhaka and processed with it. Our work uses various transfer learning deep neural network algorithms including VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetV2 for classifying road damages, as well as for detection, and it outperforms earlier research. We got the highest 97.15% accuracy for ResNet50 and lowest accuracy 94.88% for MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetV2, 94.31% accuracy for VGG16 and 93.18% for VGG19.

articleTitle: Software Defined Network Implements Real Time Detection and Mitigation of DDoS attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A Software Defined Network (SDN) controller might keep an eye on the entire network. Unquestionably, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks can affect both the controller and switch of an SDN. These kinds of attacks often target the flow tables of the deployed network switches to overwhelm the system, create substantial network delays, and consume bandwidth. Despite the number of conventional detection techniques that are already available, DDoS attacks continue to rise in rate, quantity, and amount of work done. In order to categorize DDoS attacks in an SDN simulation environment, this paper presents an analysis of the issue and makes implementation recommendations for the proposed detection and mitigation algorithm. To do this, the sFlow programme was used to simulate DDoS attacks. Experiments demonstrate that this model is highly effective at detecting security events and at real-time DDoS attack mitigation.

articleTitle: Investigation of Immersion Cooling Efficiency for Lithium-Ion Battery Pack with Machine Learning Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Battery thermal management systems play a critical role in improving their power capability, extending lifetime, and minimizing the probability of thermal runaway. These systems aim to maintain a regulated operating temperature by removing heat from the battery pack and homogenizing the temperature within and between the cells. Precisely predicting the outlet fluid temperature is crucial to enhance the efficiency and functionality of these systems through proper design and operation. In this study, we applied machine learning techniques to predict the outlet fluid temperature of immersion cooling for a lithium-ion battery pack. Nine regression models have been employed to accurately predict the outlet fluid temperature. The results indicate that the Light GBM model can significantly enhance the efficiency and performance of immersive cooling systems for Li-ion batteries. We validated our approach by comparing the predicted temperature distributions with experimental data with MAE and RMSE of 0.0136 and 0.0209, which demonstrated that our model effectively captures the heat transfer in the battery pack.

articleTitle: A Smart Mobile Application for Vehicle Tracking and Speed Warning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vehicle tracking systems are a form of technology that can be used to track an automobile using a range of techniques, including GPS, which relies on satellites and ground stations, or other techniques that depend on cell phone towers [5] [8]. In this paper an example of IoT Tracking & Speed Warning device developed that uploads vehicle data to the cloud and then makes decisions based on predetermined constraints [2]. The proposed system has three components: hardware, cloud, and android application. The hardware component is the ESP-32 which as an integrated Wi-Fi makes it easy to handle the circuit of the system [5]. The system is efficiently identifying the required information like the vehicle's speed by counting the revolutions per minute and sends an over speeding alert via the GSM module [9]. An android application is developed using android studio which establishes a secure system by giving login id and password to the owner [12]

articleTitle: Optimization with Blockchain based Secure Authentication and Collaborative Data Sharing Model in Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cloud computing has become a critical technology to meet infrastructure and data service needs cost-effectively, with minimal effort, and with a high degree of scalability. It is widespread in many facets. Although the use of cloud computing has increased significantly, concerns about information security have not yet been fully addressed. With the exponential growth of cloud computing, many new web services have emerged, making it difficult for customers to choose the services they want. This research study has attempted to create a powerful framework for data exchange called blockchain-based secure authentication and collaborative data sharing in the cloud to overcome this hurdle. The entities used in this research are third parties, data owners, smart contracts, and blockchain networks. The steps involved in this process are initialization, registration, authentication, data sharing, and decryption. The safety operators are created using Fire Hawks Optimization (FHO). In addition, the evaluation metrics are revenue, storage usage, and compute costs. Finally, the results proved that FHO-based OptiBC-SecAuth-DS achieved maximum revenue, minimum storage usage, and minimum computational costs.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Approach For Botnet Intrusion Detection System Based on Machine-Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this cyber era, the speed of technological advancements is likely linear to the constant threat to information security, one of which is the botnet attack. Recently, botnet advancement has been developing toward nowhere, where it evolves in size and sophistication. Numerous botnet Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have been developed, especially one based on network-flow detection. However, the nature of the recent botnet, equipped with advanced code updates, makes it difficult for the IDS to keep track of the botnet attack. Thus, abnormal botnet detection methods are better because they can mark a new or uncharted bot flow. This research proposes a new approach that can detect botnet types. A generic model that consists of network-flow data pre-processing and feature selection is introduced. It is then installed to the pre-known machine learning classification techniques. The model hence uses the CTU-13 dataset to measure the performance of botnet detection. Experimental results show that this proposed work works as intended in botnet detection, and the decision tree algorithm produced the best average detection accuracy of 99.02%.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Two Transformers in the Study of Plant Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper, have implement two transformer models, namely Vision Transformer (ViT) and Shifted WIndow Transformer (Swin) for identifying paddy leaf diseases at an early stage, using thermal images. Thermal images provide detailed and precise information when compared to normal images, which helps in the early detection of leaf diseases, even before the spots appear on the leaves. The aim of this paper is to prove that both Vision as well as Swin transformer works well with vision (image) tasks, such as image classification. Here, in our paper we were able to identify and classify paddy leaves diseases using ViT and swin transformer with an accuracy of 94% and 98% respectively. Swin transformer works better when it comes to semantic segmentation, where one needs to classify each pixel to it’s respective category. It does so by using the concept of Windows, about which we will talk in detail in the coming sections.

articleTitle: A Review of Lung Nodules Identification using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The identification and classification of lung nodules play a critical role in the early diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer, a leading cause of mortality worldwide. As technology advances, the integration of machine learning algorithms has emerged as a groundbreaking solution to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of lung nodule identification. This review aims to provide an overview of the recent advancements and impactful applications of Machine learning in the field of lung nodule identification. The review begins by elucidating the significance of early lung nodule detection and the challenges associated with traditional methods. It then delves into the immense potential of machine learning, which encompasses various techniques such as deep learning and convolutional neural networks. By leveraging these methods, researchers have achieved remarkable improvements in nodule detection and risk prediction. Moreover, this review highlights the role of curated datasets and various methods of lung nodule classification and segmentation. The utilisation of large-scale datasets, including publicly available datasets and clinical databases, has empowered researchers to develop robust algorithms capable of achieving exceptional performance. Furthermore, the review examines the fact that machine-learning algorithms have demonstrated the ability to identify nodules with remarkable precision. In conclusion, machine learning has emerged as a transformative force in the field of lung nodule identification, offering unprecedented accuracy and efficiency. By harnessing the power of advanced algorithms, healthcare providers can elevate their ability to detect and classify lung nodules, ultimately leading to earlier diagnosis, improved patient outcomes, and a significant reduction in lung cancer-related mortality.

articleTitle: Smartphone based skin hydration level sensor and sunburn prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Skin hydration prediction and sunburn detection are vital aspects of skin health monitoring, contributing to proactive skin care practices and prevention of potential skin damage. Sensors play a vital role in data capturing. Despite the availability of numerous sensors and smartphone applications that offer detailed information on skin health monitoring, these solutions are frequently associated with significant time consumption and high costs. As the requirement for predicting accurate results grows, the need for a larger number of records also increases, leading to computational expenses. To overcome these constraints, a streamlined approach was adopted by utilizing only two sensors: Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) for skin conductance and DHT11 for temperature and humidity. Additionally, the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) algorithm was employed, which offers the advantage of not being dependent on the number of records. This combination of a minimal sensor setup and an efficient algorithm enables effective and cost-efficient skin health monitoring by providing real-time results without compromising on the accuracy. Furthermore, the system incorporates the prediction of sunburn and calculation of vitamin D intake, a crucial aspect for maintaining optimal skin health. By providing vitamin D intake in international units, this study introduces a simplified and efficient method for generating this valuable output. This research contributes to advancing skincare practices and dermatological interventions, enabling proactive measures to mitigate the risk of sunburn and promote optimal skin health. Finally the proposed methodology exhibits promising potential for widespread adoption and future enhancements in the field of skin health monitoring.

articleTitle: The Impact of CyRIS in Ascertaining Accurate Implementation of Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This systematic review seeks to evaluate the impact of CyRIS in ascertaining accurate implementation of projects with a primary focus on the merits of its functionalities. Core to the study is the view that CyRIS-driven project implementation reduces the risks of inaccuracy to an acceptable level. Although CyRIS is an extensively researched area in cyber security, a comprehensive review of subcategories, specifically, the accurate implementation of projects using the tool remains understudied. The proposed systematic review of literature provides insights and future directions from selected databases, including ScienceDirect, Springer Journals, SAGE Journals, and Wiley Online Library. Moreover, the limitations and strengths of each article collected are assessed using the PRISMA model to identify risks of bias. The research, which consists of journal articles, conferences, and symposium papers, is analyzed using "Cyber-Range Instantiation Systems and accurate implementation of projects" as the key phrase and "Cyber-Risk Models", "Cyber Range Instantiation", and "Cyber Security Training", and "Accurate Implementation of Projects" as the keywords. The findings of the study will bridge the awareness gap in using CyRIS-led Cyber-Risk Models to execute accurate training scenarios, improve weaknesses of implementation, simulate real-time attack scenarios, and highlight existing gaps as well as prospects for future research.

articleTitle: Auto-Segmentation of Lumbar Vertebrae using MultiPlanar UNet
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vertebra segmentation is a fundamental step for spinal image analysis and interference. The lumbar backbone is critical for transferring load and permissive drive, but identifying spinal irregularities and fractures is possibly disputing. Automated medical images can assist doctors in diagnosing these environments more expertly than manual or semi-manual procedures. To advance the discovery and assessment of compression fractures utilizing MRI figures, a deep learning approach is suggested. MRI figures pose one-of-a-kind challenges due to coinciding forms and hazy boundaries, with added determinants. We propose a deep learning-based approach utilizing the MP U-Net model for segmenting individual vertebrae in MRI figures of the lumbar backbone. The ending step engages in fine-tuning the segmentation by changing the hyperparameters. This approach offers advantages over classical procedures and can potentially enhance the analysis and treatment of spinal settings.

articleTitle: Impact of Machine Learning in Music Genre Classification using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of available music tracks has made the classification of music genres increasingly crucial. To achieve accurate genre predictions, machine learning techniques have been widely employed and proven highly efficient. In this study, we focused on enhancing the accuracy of music genre classification systems by training a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model using Keras. Music genre classification serves as a valuable tool for music learning, offering a reliable method of categorization. Given the immense amount of data and the inherent complexity in identifying music genres, we leveraged the power of deep neural networks to classify ten distinct genres. To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, we compared the performance of the CNN model to other existing models using the GITZAN dataset. Our results demonstrated the success of the CNN model in accurately classifying music genres, surpassing previous studies while requiring less data. This research contributes to the field of music genre classification by providing an advanced and efficient solution using deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Optimizing Machine Learning Operators and Models for Specific Hardware Using Apache-TVM
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diligent utilization of hardware resources when dealing with computationally intensive jobs like machine learning (ML) that have a huge scope of compiler optimizations are often neglected due to the complexity of its implementation. The main reasons for its complexity is the wide range of architectures and the difference between the development and deployment environments. This leads to poor utilization of resources such as memory, hardware and increased execution time. These problems can be tackled using Apache-TVM - a compiler specifically designed to tune and optimize machine-learning models for specific hardware. We have implemented matrix multiplication on two types of hardware, x86 and Hexagon Digital Signal Processor (DSP), and have optimized it for specific hardware. Apache-TVM also supports tuning of whole ML models by applying various graph-level and operator-level optimizations. TVM can also automate the optimization of low-level programs to specific hardware characteristics using autoTVM which is a cost-based model for exploration of the search space for code optimization. We have obtained a significant reduction of upto 32.32% for Emotion FerPlus model and more than 150 times for matrix multiplication on hexagon DSP in execution time without reducing the accuracy or the performance.

articleTitle: A Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Leaf Disease Detection of Sugarcane
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Agriculture, which is closely related to the four pillars of society, is the industry that has the biggest impact on the economic development of a country. The most promising crop in India's vast array of agricultural resources is sugarcane. However, there are other difficulties that a farmer must overcome when raising these crops, such as crop illnesses, leaf problems, etc. These problems can be solved using the interesting technology known as deep learning. In order to identify and detect sugarcane leaf diseases with the highest level of accuracy feasible, this research effort integrates deep learning models. For this, a customized dataset made up of four classes has been used. The proposed modified VGG16 model was trained on an NVIDIA DGX server with RMSProp optimizer to reach a maximum accuracy of 96.50%. With the help of this research, farmers will be able to successfully combine artificial intelligence with their superior skill set to produce healthier, richer crops without worrying about these difficulties.

articleTitle: Inflammatory Bone Region Segmentation using USG Rheumatoid Arthritic Images
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurate Inflammatory bone region localization gives significant clues about the presence of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). Rheumatoid Arthritis mostly affects the smaller joints like finger and wrist joints in the early phase of the disease. Disease detection in the initial phase, is the exclusive way towards better treatment outcomes and, in the long run, reduces the degenerative effects of the disease. Advancement of the digital imaging modalities like Ultrasonography is very significant for small joint analysis like different types of hand joint those who are commonly affected by RA in early phase. The segmentation of musculoskeletal ultrasonography images is the primary important step in the early diagnosis of illnesses. In this paper, we investigated the efficiency of quality enhancement of musculoskeletal ultrasound images for segmentation of inflammatory bone regions towards diagnosis of arthritis. To meet up the specific necessities of the overall aim of this paper, firstly, various state-of-the-art quality enhancement techniques (i.e., noise reduction techniques) are implemented for quality improvement. Secondly, the performance of the state-of-the-art segmentation methods to extract the inflammatory bone line/ region from ultrasound images are investigated in terms of before and after quality enhancement. The experiments are conducted on publicly available ultrasound image dataset of arthritis patients available at: https://www.ultrasoundcases.info/. Experimental results reveal that geometric mean filtering technique (i.e., best performed enhancement technique) improves the performance of the segmentation methods for bone line segmentation.

articleTitle: An Autoencoder-based Deep Learning Approach for Classifying Colon and Rectum Adenocarcinoma
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Early identification of cancer types plays a pivotal role in administering proper therapeutics, which increases the likelihood of a favourable prognosis for cancer patients. However, distinguishing between colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and rectum adenocarcinoma (READ) samples is complex, and the classification performance of machine learning algorithms in this regard has been poor. To address this challenge, an autoencoder-based deep learning classification framework is proposed. This framework overcomes the "curse of dimensionality" problem in RNA-Seq transcriptomic data by extracting highly significant compressed-domain latent-space features for classifying COAD-READ samples. The performance of the autoencoder-based classification framework was compared with two alternative approaches using different performance measures. It was found that the MLP classifier with the autoencoder model achieves the best classification performance. Furthermore, critical hub genes and survival-associated genes in COAD-READ cancers were analyzed, and functional enrichment analysis was performed.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Methods for Prediction of Liver & Heart Diseases: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To analyze and comprehend free text, machine learning, a subset of "natural language processing," may be employed. It can be wielded in conjunction with medical data to enhance hospital triage processes, forecast patient outcomes, and flourish diagnostic algorithms that can spot early-stage chronic illnesses. As there is a greater volume of patient data to analyze in critical care and patient death prediction is widespread, these solicitations may be highly helpful. Transfer learning, a subset of "machine learning," was flourished in addition to deep learning to address the issue of large datasets. Many different medicinal contexts have wielded it. This study aims to contribute a comprehensive analysis of the development and solicitation of transfer learning in "Natural Language Processing" (NLP) methodologies, with a focus on the analysis and forecasting of diseases, particularly heart and liver problems, using clinical pictures and free-text notes. It also examines how challenging it is for NLP techniques to comprehend clinical narratives and recognize features in medical images. The search parameters for "PRISMA, or Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses", were implemented, and 31 papers were evaluated.

articleTitle: An Analytical Framework for Analyzing Tweets for Disaster Management: Case Study of Turkey Earthquake 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Citizens utilize Twitter to communicate and post useful information amid disasters. The timely analysis of the first-hand information can be valuable for enhancing disaster management. This paper presents a new analytical framework for analyzing tweets (text and images) shared during disasters to (1) identify topics discussed during a disaster from tweet text using BERTopic along with their spatiotemporal analysis (2) to assess the severity of damage from images centered on a domain adaptation (DA) approach which uses EfficientNetB4 model and an iterative self-training algorithm. Using the Turkey Earthquake 2023 as a case study, a geo-located collection of tweets shared during the earthquake is analyzed, demonstrating the framework’s usefulness in analyzing tweets related to a real-world disaster event. The proposed framework can assist to identify critical areas that require immediate attention, assess the severity of the damage, and understand the evolving situation in real-time without the requirement for labeled data.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Recurrent Implantation Failure and Pre-eclampsia Using Machine Learning and Gene Expression Profiling
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A pregnancy complication is any medical condition that arises during pregnancy that impacts the health of the mother, the fetus, or both. Recurrent implantation failure and pre-eclampsia are two such prenatal medical disorders. Machine learning systems can accurately predict high-risk prenatal medical conditions like recurrent implantation failure and pre-eclampsia. This study aimed to analyze differentially expressed genes for both pregnancy complications and develop a Machine learning model for the early prognosis of recurrent implantation failure and pre-eclampsia. Differentially expressed genes for recurrent implantation failure consisted of 2486 downregulated genes and 809 upregulated genes, and pre-eclampsia, consisted of 13 downregulated genes and 10 upregulated genes followed by gene set enrichment analysis. Gene expression prolife of recurrent implantation failure and pre-eclampsia were used to develop the machine learning model. Random Forest performed best for recurrent implantation failure with a model accuracy of 96.47%, while the generalized linear model performed best for pre-eclampsia with a model accuracy of 80%.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Inspired Automatic Road condition Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Advanced sensors for control, safety, monitoring, perception, and operation are becoming more necessary as the automobile industry undergoes rapid transformation. As computing power increases, automobiles increasingly imitate mobile computers. The quality of the roads has a significant role in determining the cost and security of transportation. In order for agencies to conduct timely repairs and maintain ideal road conditions, damage identification is a crucial duty for road maintenance. Road quality is being monitored using a variety of image and video monitoring techniques. Manually assessing and analyse incoming information may be a time-consuming process. Thus, it is important to use computer vision and deep learning methods to enhance the processes for inspecting and assessing the status of control objects. Researches have rapidly adopted object detection/classification deep learning models for road damage detection thanks to the rapid advancement of deep learning methods in recent years. Municipalities may save resources and time by using automated road damage detecting technologies. This research suggests using a CNN trained on a freshly curated dataset of road damage data from Saudi Arabia to identify the degree of road damage. Cracks, potholes, depressions, and shove are the four classified classifications presented in this study's dataset. Experts analyzed data that was obtained with the help of maintenance workers, volunteer in the city of Coimbatore using smartphones. More than one deep learning algorithm was also deployed and tested on the suggested dataset. The research shown that the suggested custom CNN (RoadNet) outperformed the per-trained models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: SAF-NET: Split Attention Fusion Network for retinal vessel segmentation from fundus images
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Regular analysis of retinal vessels can alert the occurrence of many retinal pathological disorders like Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) and Glaucoma in their early stages. In view of this, a robust deep learning model, called the Split Attention-Fusion Network (SAF-Net) is implemented using two subnetworks to detect and generate two probabilistic maps for arteries and veins respectively. The first subnetwork is a modified version of U-Net and acts as a backbone for SAF-Net and extracts the most pertinent feature maps to detect the major blood vessels. Further, to detect the tiny vessel and branch junction pixels, an effective residual-like structured block named Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (MSFF) is proposed. The feature maps of both subnetworks are concatenated to produce the final segmented maps of retinal blood vessels with high precision. The efficacy of proposed SAF-Net model is evaluated using two standard publicly available datasets (Dualmodel2019 and AV datasets) and one local real-time dataset.

articleTitle: Prediction of PCOD using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Women of reproductive age are disproportionately affected by polycystic ovary disease (PCOD), a prevalent endocrine condition. This disorder is sometimes referred to as polycystic ovary disease. About 5 million women of childbearing age throughout the globe have polycystic ovary disease (PCOD). As a consequence, the ovaries may enlarge or form many cysts. Acne, greasy skin, hirsutism (an abnormal development in female sexual characteristics), and increased facial hair are only some of the potential adverse effects. These symptoms often accompany this illness. The pathophysiology of polycystic ovary disease (PCOD) is poorly understood now. Ovarian involvement is central to the diagnostic criteria for this disease. The development of PCOD is influenced by both hereditary and environmental factors. Using machine learning that has been trained on large quantities of data from clinical practice, this disease may be detected. As a solution, we present a set of statistically-analysed optimum and minimum parameters. This approach may help during the early diagnosis and therapy prediction of PCOD based on these parameters. The solution was created using a number of machine-learning methods. Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Classifier, Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBRF, and CatBoost Classifier were some of the methods used.

articleTitle: Review on Writer Identification and Verification Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Biometric authentication requires identifying patterns based on unique behavioral or physiological characteristics. The most commonly considered physiological biometric systems are fingerprint scanning and facial recognition. Behavioral biometric systems are signature, handwriting, and voice recognition. Verifying physical features occurs efficiently through comparison, whereas recognizing behavioral components presents a challenge. Among the different biometric modalities, writer identification and verification have garnered considerable interest because of their potential to improve accuracy and reliability of authentication systems. Writer verification forms the legal basis for documents such as wills, contracts, and suicide notes. Handwriting verification tasks require years of training, and handwriting analysis is time-consuming. Therefore, researchers have tried to build accurate and efficient writer identification and verification systems. Researchers over the decades have explored various approaches for writer identification and verification tasks, including traditional machine learning methodologies and, more recently, deep learning methods. This review paper presents an informative summary of the databases, preprocessing methods, feature extraction techniques, and classifiers employed in identifying and verifying writers. While writer authentication has shown promising results, further research is needed to address several challenges in this task.

articleTitle: A Perspective way of designing Intelligent systems with Face Detection and Recognition using Artificial Intelligence for Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project proposes an AI-based approach for face detection and recognition using YOLOv4 and CNN. It aims to be used in various applications like security systems and automatic attendance marking in educational institutions. Traditional machine learning methods like FaceNet and MTCNN have not achieved satisfactory accuracy. Hence, deep learning techniques are employed. YOLO, a deep learning library, is utilized for implementation. The key steps include creating an effective dataset, labeling images with faces using LabelImg software, and training the dataset using Google Colab GPU. The trained dataset is used to mark bounding boxes around faces in images or real-time video. The YOLOv4 technique is implemented using the darknet framework. Around 20 images are used for testing, resulting in an approximate accuracy of 85% due to the high accuracy of YOLOv4.

articleTitle: A Transfer-Learning Based Unbiased Voting Bone Cancer Detection Framework from Histological Osteosarcoma Images
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The most lethal types of bone cancer, osteosarcoma, have a substantially higher fatality rate for the child. The clinician’s labor can be significantly decreased and patient outcomes may be enhanced by using computer vision-based technology. A paradigm for the hard-voting, impartial identification of bone cancer is presented in our study. A histological osteosarcoma image dataset with three separate groups that is publicly available is employed in this research. A comparison of the models developed from balanced and unbalanced training sets has been accomplished using seven customized deep transfer learning algorithms, including VGG19, MobileNetV1, MobileNetV2, ResNetV250, InceptionV2, NasNetMobile, and EfficientNetV2-B0. Kappa scores and accuracy are foremost for MobileNetV2 and those are 87.55% and 92.14% respectively. In contrast, the creative Max Voting classifier eventually integrates a number of weakly performing transfer learning classifiers and exhibits robust performance on malignant categories. The Max voting classifier outperforms other existing models. The accuracy rate of the Max Voting classifier is 93.88%.

articleTitle: Motion Prediction for Autonomous Vehicles Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles require motion prediction of nearby traffic agents to guarantee secure navigation. By anticipating the movements of surrounding objects such as other vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles, the autonomous vehicle can make informed decisions to prevent collisions, adjust speed and direction, and operate effectively in changing conditions. Motion prediction is an essential aspect of autonomous vehicle systems, contributing to increased safety, dependability, and efficiency. This work generates an effective mechanism to predict the movement direction of nearby traffic entities around our ego vehicle (the vehicle that we originally reference) using deep learning techniques and the inclusion of a LIDAR-based dataset.

articleTitle: Comparative Survey of Various Intelligent Methods for Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cancer remains a major contributor to mortality rates across the globe, causing nearly 10 million fatalities in 2020. Among all cancer types, breast cancer has the highest incidence, around 2.26 million cases reported across the globe by the World Health Organization. In the last few years, breast cancer was diagnosed in approximately 2.3 million people and caused around 685,000 deaths. In this paper, our investigation entails executing a statistical scrutiny of the worldwide proliferation of breast cancer, as well as delving into various machine learning and deep learning techniques for detecting breast cancer, along with their constraints and intricacies. Additionally, we have proposed a hybrid Machine Learning (ML) approach for detecting breast cancer with utmost accuracy, which streamlines the assessment procedure presently employed by radiologists in screening mammograms.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Renal CT Image Classification Using Convolution Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Computer tomography (CT), also known as computed tomography, is a medical imaging method that generates detailed and precise horizontal or axial images of targeted regions of the body for diagnostic purposes. In this particular study, the focus was on performing image classification of CT scan images of the Kidney. This organ plays an essential role in detoxification, fluid balance, and maintaining electrolyte levels in the human body. The dataset used for the study contained 12,446 images into four labeled classes - Cyst, Tumor, Stone, and Normal. Convolution Neural Network (CNN) model is built for binary (Normal and Tumor) and multi-image Classification to classify the Renal CT images into four classes. CNN uses ReLU as an activation function for classifying these images.
