This study examines the performance of four multiclass brain tumor identification algorithms utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), VGG-16, MobileNetV2, and InceptionV3. The dataset comprises 3264 images of four types of brain cancers (glioma, meningioma, pituitary, and no tumor). The images are pre-processed and then analyzed by the algorithms. The results demonstrate that CNN obtains the highest accuracy of 95%, followed by VGG-16 at 93%, MobileNetV2 at 91%, and InceptionV3 at 89%. This study illustrates the efficiency of CNN in detecting brain cancers and sets a benchmark for future research on the subject.

articleTitle: Soft Computing Approach To Prevent Derailments Due To Landslides
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Our country has a large network of railways. There is about 115000 km of railway tracks in our country. The United Nations has the largest network of railways followed by China and India. Sometimes the tracks are laid between the mountains. In India about 420km of the railway tracks are laid across the mountains. There is a possibility for landslides in such hilly areas. These landslides can result in the derailment of the train which leads to the tragic accidents. Records show that about 70% of the rail derailments happen due to the landslides. Hence there is a necessity of detecting the landslides in prior to the tragic accidents. There is no existing system for detecting such landslides in prior nevertheless there are systems to detect the cracks in the railway track. But this system cannot detect the landslides in prior, hence a new system with these features added is required. The system proposed here focuses on predicting the landslides priorly and hence send the warning message to the nearby station and the engine driver. The fuzzy toolbox in MATLAB is used here for the simulation of this paper. The reasons for the landslides were studied and the possible measures of predicting the landslides are studied. This paper briefly elaborates the methods involved in the prediction of the landslides occurrence and thereby warn the concerned personnel. The proposed system is 81.9% accurate.

articleTitle: A Relative Weight-Based Fuzzy k-Nearest Neighbour Classifier for Chemical Analysis of Wine and Glass Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The nearest neighbour (NN) classifier is a widely used classifier that classifies a test pattern based on the class of its closest neighbour. The NN classifier has several variants, namely k-NN, modified k-NN (Mk-NN) and fuzzy k-NN (Fk-NN). These variants classify a test pattern using some or all of the training patterns. The k-NN classifier is different from the Mk-NN classifier in terms of weight, whereas the Mk-NN classifier is different from the Fk-NN classifier in terms of membership value. This paper introduces a new classifier called relative weight-based Fk-NN (RWFk-NN) by taking advantage of Mk-NN and Fk-NN classifiers. It also presents a comparative analysis of these classifiers using three techniques, namely k-fold cross-validation, k-test analysis and m-test analysis, on the wine and glass identification datasets from the University of California Irvine (UCI) machine learning repository. The performance of all the classifiers is measured in terms of accuracy. The findings reveal that the RWFk-NN classifier outperforms all the other classifiers in both datasets.

articleTitle: Implementation of Optimized Logic Gate Circuits with Majority Voter using QCA Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) is one of the most promising nanotechnologies for overcoming the inadequacies of Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) technology. QCA provides a very efficient computational platform. It is most alluring due to its features, speed, size, minimal power drain, high scalable and higher switching frequency. This paper presents the construction of fundamental, universal and hybrid gates using QCA Majority Voter and the results are in contrast to CMOS logic circuits. The designs are efficient over CMOS logic in terms of area and delay. Authors proposed a straightforward to implement and are having no wire crossings to implement. With the help of a Majority Voter these circuits are realized and also implement any digital circuit using QCA. It is done by using the QCA designer 2.0.3 tool. These circuits are simulated and tested by applying some test inputs to ensure they produce the intended results.

articleTitle: Refining RNMC compensation for Three Stage Amplifier using DTMOS Transistor and FFVF
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, Reversed Nested Miller Compensation (RNMC) is refined by including DTMOS transistor in first stage. Further, a Folded Flipped Voltage Follower (FFVF) is put forward in inner loop to alleviate the RHP zero issue. A resistor is placed in the outer loop to enhance the phase margin by double pole-zero cancellation. The large signal response is taken care of by the feed forward path. The functionality is confirmed via simulations in Tanner tool by taking TSMC 0.18 µm CMOS technology parameters. The gain-bandwidth product (GBW) is found to be 33.3 MHz which is considerably better than contemporaries and phase margin (PM) is observed as 54°. The slew rate (SR) is 9.71 V/µS. Figure of merits are also computed to characterize the performance of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: The Spread of Malicious Activity in a Computer Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Computer networks have become increasingly vulnerable to malicious activity due to the proliferation of malicious software. Malware, ransomware, phishing attacks, and other cyber threats can spread rapidly through interconnected systems, causing significant harm to individuals, businesses, and even governments. This paper aims to investigate the different types of cyber threats and the methods by which they spread in a computer network. By examining recent case studies, we will analyze the impact of these cyber threats and discuss best practices for preventing and mitigating their spread. Malicious activity can spread rapidly through interconnected systems, resulting in significant consequences for individuals, businesses, and even governments. This paper aims to explore the different types of cyber threats and the methods by which they spread in a computer network. By examining recent case studies, we will analyze the impact of cyber threats and discuss best practices for preventing and mitigating their spread. An investigation of short-term immunity among computer nodes in a broad network is presented in this paper using the compartmental infection model. This computational model has been validated by inferential simulations.

articleTitle: A Heuristic Approach to Identify Influential Node in Complex Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Multiple features of the complex network are exhibited among the nodes in time-varying social networks. Community detection has numerous approaches, but the majority of methods are restricted to disjoint community situations. Solutions to disjoint community situations do not reflect well on real-world social networks. An innovative heuristic method has been proposed to recognize community structure in real-world networks and to identify the most influential node within each community. The proposed concept on a recognized community network has been tested in order to validate it. This work introduced one new network metric, the Dependency factor which computes the influence of a node. Our results are compared with other existing approaches using real-life datasets. We have compared the dependency factor with other network centralities. The computational case study is done over a well-known Bengali novel, namely Chaar Adhyay written by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore. The analytical results are more accurate than the state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Nilearn-based Multimodal Fusion Analysis for Integrating Brain Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The integration of multiple brain imaging modalities has become a prominent research approach for understanding complex neural processes. The present study focuses on the application of Nilearn, a Python library for neuroimaging analysis in multimodal fusion analysis. The aim is to combine data from different modalities, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetoencephalography (MEG), to gain comprehensive insights into brain function. The research article presents a detailed workflow using Nilearn for multimodal fusion analysis. Two key multimodal fusion techniques, joint independent component analysis (jICA) and connectome-based fusion, implemented using Nilearn, are discussed in detail in this study. The workflow presented provides researchers with a systematic approach to integrate and interpret brain imaging data, facilitating a deeper understanding of the complex neural mechanisms underlying brain function and connectivity.

articleTitle: Smart Monitoring and Automated PH Controlled System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A pH automation system using Arduino is a project that utilizes the Arduino microcontroller board to automate pH measurement and control in various applications such as hydroponics, aquaponics, and water treatment. The system employs pH sensors to determine if a solution is acidic or alkaline, and depending on the results, it can change the solution's pH by operating a pump or valve that supplies pH adjuster solutions. The Arduino board serves as the brain that analyses the pH data from the sensor, determines the necessary pH adjustment, and activates the pump or valve to perform the modifications. The system can be programmed with specific setpoints for pH levels, allowing for precise control over the pH of the solution. The pH automation system can improve the efficiency and accuracy of pH control in various applications, and the use of Arduino allows for a cost-effective and customizable solution. However, it is important to note that the system's effectiveness depends on the accuracy and calibration of the pH sensors used.

articleTitle: Structural analysis using MPU6050 gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Many buildings are sensitive to earthquake and hurricanes, and it is easy to generate large deflection and dynamic response even through daily motion of a huge crowd. There are also structures with inappropriate distributions of strength and stiffness which performs poorly in case of any seismic activity and are one of the major causes of collapses leading to loss of lives. With these issues, there is a growing demand for the exploration of different methodologies to detect the prime areas in the structures that require improvement and repair, and with these early detection techniques, we can take suitable action that can, in turn, save a lot of lives. Previous research in this field mainly revolved around checking concrete strength and rust which was insufficient. Other devices which exist are expensive and they has to be equipped while constructing the building. In this paper we have summarised our study on finding the structural strength of buildings with the help of MPU6050 gyroscope. The MPU6050 gyroscope is a 3-axis gyroscope and a 3-axis accelerometer. The sensor measures the angular rotation from its axis and transfers it to the smartphone using a Bluetooth module.

articleTitle: Blinkify – A IoT Based Device for Speech Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The discovery and popularity that came by, for the Internet of Things have made life more inclusive and productive for people with speech disabilities caused because of motor neuron diseases like ALS. Such people have no means or are sometimes excluded from the usual walk of life. Most invented intelligent detection devices, including portable devices for people with disabilities in speech, are costly and unaffordable for patients in underdeveloped and developing countries. Blinkify is an IoT technology-based wearable device, which uses modified Morse code for communication. Motor neuron disease-affected patients can use this device for communication by means of eye blinking. The device tracks this eye blinks and converts it into Morse code, which is transmitted to a mobile or laptop connected to the system. It also provides a secure pathway for communication. With the added benefits of easy handling, low cost and easy portability, it becomes immensely useful for people who are paralyzed and cannot communicate by mouth or sign. The system also requires less assistance from another person.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cardiac Illness using Machine Learning Algorithms with and without Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predicting cardiac disease is a major challenge in medicine, as it is the leading cause of death worldwide, accounting for approximately 31% of all fatalities. Early detection and treatment of cardiac disorders is difficult, especially in poor countries where diagnostic facilities and qualified medical professionals may be lacking. The diagnostic process can also be time-consuming and complex, with medical experts relying on empirical data to make a patient's diagnosis more certain.To address this challenge, the researchers aim to use various algorithms, such as LDA, RF, GBC, DT, SVM, and KNN, along with XGBoost, Voting Classifier, MLP-ANN, and SMO, as well as feature selection techniques like SFS and RFE, with and without Feature Selection. The performance of these ten algorithms will be compared using the Datasets for Cleveland, Hungary, Switzerland, and Long Beach V, as well as the Dataset Heart Statlog, with the K-fold cross-validation approach used for verification. The front-end of the model will be developed using the Flask framework in Python, and users will log in and enter the necessary data to predict the illness. The main goal of this project is to develop a novel modelling technique that builds on previous work, as well as to create a model that is user-friendly and easily implementable in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection using Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have revolutionized various industries, including the medical field. Deep learning algorithms are being used in medical science for diagnosis making it faster and more accurate. This study utilizes deep learning techniques for detection of brain tumor using MRI scans of human brain. The research work utilizes a publicly available database of MRI images of brain tumors including Pituitary, Glioma and Meningioma brain tumors. The image enhancement step consists of noise removal technique using Gaussian Filter, followed by Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) for contrast adjustment and Contour creation for refining edges. For detection different neural network architectures have been used - ResNet 152, Xception, VGG 16, Inception V3 and MobileNet V2, with ImageNet weights to classify the diseases. The models outperform the previously proposed methods and achieves the best accuracy of 98.039% by Xception architecture.

articleTitle: A Robust Approach for Malaria Parasite Identification with CNN Based Feature Extraction and Classification using SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Malaria is a fatal illness caused by the transmission of the Plasmodium parasite through Anopheles mosquitoes. It causes symptoms like fever, chill, headache, and fatigue. In severe cases, it also leads to organ failure and death. The conventional method of detecting malaria is through microscopy. The development of new tools and algorithms for malaria diagnosis and treatment is crucial. In this study, a CNN-based model has been proposed for the feature extraction from raw thin blood smear images. The extracted features are then classified into one of the four species types of namely Falciparum, Vivax, Ovale and Malariae using an SVM classifier. The proposed model achieves a significantly good accuracy of 98%, demonstrating the effectiveness of deep learning techniques in Malaria diagnosis and species classification. This study has significant implications for the development of new tools for Malaria diagnosis and treatment, which could help to speed up the process of detection and help the medical practitioner make an accurate analysis of infection, particularly in rural areas, where medical facilities are scarce.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a configurable Asynchronous Sample-Rate Converter for Digital Audio
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Most of the modern SoC designs have multiple functional and processing blocks and all operating at different sampling rate, hence arises the need of sample rate converters. In digital-audio ASICs, it is very common to change the sampling rate by a factor (int or frac) to match a downstream block. This work mainly focuses on designing and implementing sample rate converters for conversions between arbitrary sample rates in between different blocks on a chip. The design of an ASRCs for digital-audio applications is presented here, which has a variable ratio based on the need. The sample rate of each block on-chip can be changed as per user choice as the ASRC is designed with configurable register controls.

articleTitle: Real time Air Writing and Recognition of Tamil Characters with voice integration using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, a real time air writing and recognition system for Tamil alphabets using deep learning has been proposed. Air-writing is writing characters in the free space using fingers. The trajectory of the air written characters is mapped by using Media Pipe Function. The obtained trajectory is then pre-processed and given to Dense Net 121 which is a type of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model widely used for pattern matching along with the dataset from HP labs which contains 18215 images for 11 uyir ezhuthugal, 18 mei ezhuthugal,5 vada mozhi ezhuthugal and 1 aayudha ezhuthu. The model which is trained and obtained a maximum training and validation accuracy of 83.58% and 93.53% respectively with minimum training and validation loss of 478.45% and 19.7% respectively with F1 score of 0.9355.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Objective Optimization of Latent Variables in Variational Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper discusses experiments on variational autoencoders (VAE) to analyze the partwise optimization of the latent vector with multiple objective functions in the context of speech enhancement. The latent vector as a whole is optimized for the VAE objective, which is the reconstruction of noisy speech feature vectors. Simultaneously, a part of the latent vector is optimized for speech enhancement and frame-based phoneme classification. Relevant datasets are used to benchmark any impact of the frame classifier on speech enhancement. We report that the optimization of the latent vector part for frame-based phoneme classification doesn’t impact speech enhancement at low SNR speech input and adversely affects speech enhancement at relatively high SNR speech input.

articleTitle: Analysing Facial Emotion for Children with Autism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Autism is a developmental disorder that affects how people communicate and connect with one another. It can be challenging for autistic children to comprehend and express their emotions. To address this, we will use a game to capture and analyze the facial expressions of children with autism. The goal of the game is to be engaging and interactive, with different tasks that evoke different emotions. The facial expressions of the children will be analyzed using a technology that can identify different emotions based on facial expressions. We will provide valuable insights into the emotional state of children with autism during different tasks, which can help caregivers and therapists to customize interventions and track progress. It has the potential to improve the social communication and emotional understanding of children with autism, leading to a better quality of life for them and their families.

articleTitle: Exploring KD Trees and KNN Search in the context of Google Maps: An Insightful Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study suggests using a genetic algorithm to determine the shortest path between any two points on a map. The suggested method uses the longitude as well as the latitude of a present location to anticipate and pinpoint the closest cities and includes the ideas of the crossover and mutation to create novel approaches. The suggested genetic algorithm technique surpasses standard algorithms in terms of quality of solution and computing performance, according to experimental data. The suggested method gives a fresh answer to the shortest route on a map and sheds light on the application of genetic methods in this situation.

articleTitle: Stock Market Graph Prediction using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: There has been a rapid growth in the number of traders and investors in the stock market. A lot of them are beginners and young adults with little to no knowledge about the stock market. So it is essential to help these people out to minimise their losses and increase their profits while investing. A predicted graph of a particular stock in the stock market can help them do so. This paper focuses on the machine learning algorithm: Long Short-Term Memory to predict the graphs of a particular stock. The data is fetched from Yahoo Finance to get accurate results from the historic data. The website that has been made is very accessible for all kinds of users. It provides them with a simple input field to enter the stock to generate the predicted graph of the stock they wish to look for. It also shows the users if a stock is bullish (prices will rise) or bearish (prices will fall) for the particular week and month for their better understanding. The website also features a news section which highlights news and information related to the stock market and also the factors that affect the trends in the stock market.

articleTitle: Poze with Vogue
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: We present a poze and attire recommendation system that guides a user in how to best pose while taking a picture and provides the best alternatives for their attire as well as for their poses. Given an input image the system provides most attractive poses and trending fashion attire. Recommendation results in the system are influenced by the appearance and initial pose of the input image. Additionally, the user study indicates that the performance of the recommendation system is moderately correlated with the degree of conformity among the recommendations provided by different photographers. This suggests that the system takes into account factors such as image appearance and pose to generate tailored recommendations. It likely analyzes these aspects to determine the most suitable suggestions for a given image. In this project we have used human pose estimation model that provides thirty-three body point coordinates of an individual in a particular image. We have used a dataset containing insights from images using the above stated model. We have used both supervised and unsupervised learning for getting the best suggestions according to the user. At present, there are many image editing tools that provides some filters, and image enhancement techniques that can be used to beautify the already clicked image but there is no such application that provides posture suggestions while capturing the image. Therefore, this application is the first one in the field.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Mammogram Classification to Detect Breast Cancer using Boosted PSO Feature Selection and Multi-Feature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Breast cancer is a globally recognized public health issue, particularly impacting women. While mammogram screening is a widely used method for identifying cancerous cells, accurately distinguishing these cells from the surrounding tissue remains a challenge. A novel approach is presented in this study, to categorize mammograms. Initially, preprocessing is done by median filter with Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE). Multi-Feature Analysis (MFA) is used for feature extraction to extract texture, shape, and volume information from the mammograms. A Modified Weighted Particle Swarm Optimization (MWPSO) algorithm selects the optimal features, which are fed to the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light GBM) for classification. The model's performance is evaluated through k-fold cross-validation and demonstrates high accuracy in mammogram classification. By combining the strengths of image processing and machine learning algorithms, the proposed methodology provides a powerful tool for mammogram classification.

articleTitle: AMRDB: Design of an automatic analytical model for density-based clustering using augmented rule mining
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Density based clustering (DBC) is an unsupervised learning method which is capable of identifying distinct groups of information. It works on the principle of instance-based variance maximization between distinct groups, while minimizing variance between similar groups of data. DBC models are capable of detecting regions of similar concentrated instances, and discard sparse instances based on pre-set distance ratios. Thus, selection of this distance ratio must be done intelligently in order to perform effective density-based clustering. A wide range of models are proposed for this purpose, but most of them work in a context-dependent manner, thereby limiting their scalability. In order to remove this drawback, an augmented rule mining approach that utilizes a combination of Apriori and frequent pattern growth (FPGrowth) is proposed in this text. The proposed approach initially evaluates minimum support values for Apriori & FPGrowth models via variance-based analytical modelling. Rules for these models are combined using instance-based matching, and are used for parametric tuning of Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) model. Due to a combination of Apriori & FPGrowth a large number of rules are extracted in a dataset-independent manner, which assist in optimization of DBSCAN’s inter-class and intra-class variance metrics. The results are compared with various state-of-the-art clustering models, and cluster metrics are evaluated. It is observed that the proposed model outperforms DBSCAN, and other density-based clustering techniques in terms of cluster formation efficiency, scalability and computational complexity on multiple datasets.

articleTitle: Performance of NOMA over Shadowed Fading Channels with Impact of Co-channel Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) holds great promise for future wireless communications. This study investigates the inter- and intra-cell interference’s effects on the multi-user (MU) NOMA-based communication system’s outage performance. We initially checked for interference from neighbouring Voronoi cells to assess the likelihood of an outage before accounting for different channel propagation effects including fading, shadowing, and a combination of the two. We start with Rayleigh fading and log-normal shadowing to get a closed-form formula for the outage probability. We determine the outage for two users, such as a nearby user and an edge user, in a Voronoi cell. The resulting expressions are usefull for evaluating the effects of interference on the operation of the NOMA system with various fading and shadowing characteristics. The findings are quite gratifying in contrast to the simulated NOMA.

articleTitle: Deduction of efficient algorithm to anatomize job insights
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this model, freshers, job seekers, as well as other professionals, are given the opportunity to know what is new in the market through a platform that enables them to keep up with the newest technology. We will be extracting data from job portals like Naukri, LinkedIn, etc., which analyzes and optimizes the data using machine learning algorithms. This optimized data will provide better insights and will be helpful in different ways. Beautiful Soup and Selenium web drivers are used to scrape and extract data from an open website. In order to extract the precise data, we are comparing the classification algorithms and choosing the most accurate one to implement. This will help in analyzing web data and providing better insights. We also added an additional section called Find-Jobs, which helps people to find jobs based on their location, experience, and designation.

articleTitle: Gold-coated Dual Polarized Highly Sensitive Photonic Crystal Fiber based Plasmonic Biosensor: Numerical Investigation and Design
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this study, we carried out a numerical investigation to evaluate the performance of highly sensitive photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based plasmonic biosensors for refractive index sensing. A small layer of gold is applied to the fiber's exterior, acting as a plasmonic material that enhances chemical stability by reducing the likelihood of oxidation. The study employed the finite element method (FEM) for designing and analyzing various geometric parameters impact on the sensing capabilities of the biosensor. The proposed biosensor can detect refractive index changes within the range of 1.33 to 1.40, exhibiting the highest wavelength sensitivities of 21000 nmRIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 24000 nmRIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and the highest amplitude sensitivities of 2112 /RIU, 1438 /RIU for x- and y-polarization modes, respectively. Moreover, the sensor exhibits a high resolution of 4.7619×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> and 4.16667×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> RIU, respectively, for x- and y-polarization modes. The promising findings and broad range of detection abilities suggest that the proposed sensor would be appropriate for detecting biological and biochemical samples.

articleTitle: Writer Identification from Offline Handwriting Images in Urdu Script with Dense-Net: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Handwriting serves as a valuable tool in various organizational processes, such as recruitment, interviewing, team-building, counseling, and career planning. Even identical twins with identical genes exhibit distinct handwriting styles. Leveraging this uniqueness, systems that can classify handwriting can determine the identity, age, handedness, nationality, and other details of the writer, making it an effective and reliable indicator of personality and behavior. Writer identification systems, for instance, can identify writers based on their distinct handwriting patterns. Manual extraction of handwriting features from a large dataset was once nearly impossible, but thanks to deep learning algorithms, it is now feasible to automatically extract features from documents and accurately predict the author's identity. However, there is a dearth of such systems for Urdu script, as evidenced by the literature survey. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a CNN-based model, Dense-Net, as a writer identification system trained and tested on an offline Urdu handwritten dataset contributed by 418 Urdu writers. Our model achieved an impressive overall accuracy of 99.20%, outperforming all existing methods for writer identification systems.

articleTitle: Fluid Flow Monitoring and Pipeline Fault Diagnosis in Three Tank Conical System Based on Capsule Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Fluid flow monitoring and pipeline fault diagnosis are crucial tasks in various industrial processes to ensure efficient and safe operation. Capsule Neural Network (Caps Net) used to present a novel method to ensure consistent fluid flow by diagnosis the pipeline fault in a three-tank conical tank system. Flow is continuously monitored based upon the measurement and control of pressure using Distributed Control System (DCS) and continuously monitoring its variation. A comprehensive dataset comprising sensor measurements and fault labels is used to train the Caps Net. Experimental findings show that the suggested approach is effective at identifying and categorizing problems such leaking, blockage, and valve dysfunction. The Caps Net exhibits robustness against noise and variations in operating conditions. This approach has practical implications for industrial systems, improving reliability, reducing downtime, and minimizing repairs.

articleTitle: Covid-19 Detection using chest X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: COVID-19 is a virus which is a type of contagious virus it spread from one person to another person. It has symptoms like high fever, cold, and cough. In studies, it has been discovered that covid causes a vigorous effect on the lung i.e., there must be some opacity in the lungs. So, chest X-ray images can be used to detect Covid. This study aims to detect both covid and pneumonia patients, with more accuracy. The dataset consists of 576 images of Covid patients, 4273 Pneumonia patients, and 1583 Normal patients. In this study, deep learning algorithms are used. Keras is used for forming the framework of the neural network, CNN is used for image classification, drop out layer is used for preventing overfitting and Ensembling is used to create subset of the model and gain accuracy. The model able to detect accurately whether a patient is having pneumonia or covid even in the presence of inconsistent data. The accuracy achieved by the model is 96%.

articleTitle: PCA-KNN Classifier for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy: A Study on Prostate Cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most prevalent cancer worldwide and the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in males. Screening tests like the Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test and Digital Rectal Exam (DRE) are used for diagnosis. However, the raw screening dataset obtained from the National Cancer Institute's Cancer Data Access System (CDAS) posed challenges due to high dimensionality and null values. To address this, we employed data pre-processing and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimension reduction, resulting in a standardized dataset. The transformed dataset was then classified using k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The proposed classifier achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 97.35%, demonstrating its efficacy in classification tasks. This study highlights the potential of PCA for data pre-processing and the effectiveness of KNN in accurately classifying prostate cancer screening data. The findings contribute valuable insights to enhance diagnosis and decision-making in prostate cancer management.

articleTitle: Fractal Geometry-Based On-Chip Inductors for High-Frequency Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: On-chip inductors constitute key components in RF and high-frequency circuits, and in recent years, their miniaturization has been an essential area of research. Fractal geometries are becoming an effective solution to the limitations of conventional inductor designs as they offer improved performance and increased miniaturization. This review paper presents an overview of the design and performance analysis of on-chip fractal inductors. Various fractal geometries such as as Sierpinski, Koch, Minkowski, and Hilbert curves based on-chip fractal inductors are examined. Performance metrics for on-chip fractal inductors, such as inductance, Q factor, and self-resonance frequency, are reviewed. This review paper presents a detailed analysis of the current state-of-the-art in on-chip fractal inductors, emphasizing their potential to be a key component of contemporary fields.

articleTitle: Dissecting the Convolutional Neural Networks via Activation Maps for agricultural rice grain quality prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: There has been a meteoric rise in the application of AI during the past decade. Researchers are looking into using AI algorithms in almost every domain. AI algorithms are being used in modern agricultural research and practices for a variety of tasks, from quality control to increasing agricultural production. Using Deep Learning algorithms can be difficult because of their heuristic character. Class Activation based approaches like CAM and Gradient based CAM have emerged and greatly improved the model's explainability. In this paper we have classified rice grain based on their images and showed that the convolutional neural networks capture the shape of these grains for the classification task based on their quality whereas researchers have use morphological based features for classifying the rice grains based on their quality. We have used Grad-CAM, to show that the CNN captures the shape of the rice grains. We have explored state of the art CNN architectures like AlexNet, ResNet18 and VGG-16 along with a four convolutional layer CNN for the work. We show how the Grad-CAM localizes the shape of the various rice grains and the class for which it fails.

articleTitle: Detecting Contradiction and Entailment in Multilingual Text
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With many applications, including text categorization, question-and-answer systems, and sentiment mapping, entailment and contradiction detection in multilingual content is a crucial task in the discipline of natural language processing. This study examines the capabilities of two advanced models, the BERT-based multilingual case model and the XLM-RoBERTa large model, in detecting entailment and contradiction in a multilingual dataset containing 15 diverse languages. While the initial performance of BERT and XLM-RoBERTa models was 30% and 40% respectively, we have successfully enhanced the XLM-RoBERTa model’s accuracy to an impressive 70% using data processing techniques. These results imply that, by carefully selecting models and employing the relevant data processing techniques, it is possible to detect contradiction and entailment in multilingual text with high accuracy. The study’s outcomes are relevant to various areas of natural language processing, including the analysis of multilingual text. These results lay the groundwork for future studies in language processing and can guide the development of more sophisticated models.

articleTitle: Design of Dynamic comparator using CMOS and FINFET technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A two-stage and three-stage dynamic comparator architecture is proposed using FINFET technology for high speed, low power dissipation and comparison is done between three-stage and two-stage dynamic comparators with and without tail transistors. The designed comparator compares the two analog input voltage signals and generates the greater signal as the output. FINFET technology is used to overcome the short-channel effects in CMOS. In this paper the FINFET is designed with different supply voltages and analyzed power dissipation and delay. The comparison with tail and without tail of two-stage and three-stage comparators specifies that the delay and power dissipation has been reduced greatly with tail transistor. Two-stage, Three-stage Dynamic Comparator are designed and simulated in HSPICE using 16nm and 20nm CMOS and FINFET technologies.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Energy Efficient Single Junction Photovoltaic Cell with Nanostructured Zinc Oxide (ZnO) based Antireflection Coating and performance Comparison with Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) based Antireflection Coated Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The detailed study on this research includes in the fabrication of Zinc oxide based photovoltaic cells with efficiency enhancement using Finite Difference Time Domain Technique comparing the efficiency of Zinc oxide based photovoltaic cell with Indium tin oxide based photovoltaic cells at different cell thickness ranges from 40 nm to 600 nm. The two configurations of the single junction photovoltaic cell are ZnO and ITO as Antireflection coating. Each group consists of 15 samples which are simulated using a nano hub simulation tool. Group 1 is a ZnO based PV cell and Group 2 is ITO based PV cell. The G power calculation is carried out with the required number of samples with a minimum power fixed at a confident interval of 80% and permissible error of 5%. On simulating both solar cell devices by using nano hub online simulation tool, the efficiency of the ZnO based single junction photovoltaic cell is 20.37 % and 18.91 % for the ITO based single junction photovoltaic cell. The significance is 0.003. From the extensive works, it is observed that Single junction photovoltaic cells with ZnO as an anti-reflection coating shows higher performance than ITO based single junction photovoltaic cells.

articleTitle: Attention to Traffic: Network Traffic Classification using Attention-Based CNNs
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Due to the worldwide lockdown amidst the COVID-19 crisis, which forced companies, individuals as well as network infrastructures to adapt to the new normal of Work From Home (WFH), Internet Service Providers (ISPs) reported about a 60% increase in Internet traffic when compared to with the data before the pandemic. Consequently, network traffic categorization has become a critical topic in computer networking since it is crucial for activities like bandwidth allocation, resource management, intrusion detection, and virus detection. This work attempts to predict network flows’ bandwidth need and duration using the public QUIC dataset. Many applications benefit from knowing the bandwidth demand and duration. They allow for efficient resource allocation, a better quality of service and faster routing. In the past, traditional ML approaches, such as SVM and Random Forest algorithms as well as deep learning algorithms, such as Deep Clustering, have been implemented to solve the problem of network traffic classification. We show that our Attention-Based Convolutional Neural Network outperforms existing approaches which have relied on traditional Machine Learning, Transfer Learning and Multitask Learning techniques. The proposed model achieves accuracy scores of 96% (Bandwidth data) and 94.30% (Duration data) for five-class classification. We observe a significant increase of up to 6% compared to previous results.

articleTitle: A Critical Study of Challenges and Risk in Healthcare sector based on Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cloud computing has been critical to the world's modern technological growth. Cloud computing is one of the most advantageous solutions to digital challenges. Security is a major concern in cloud computing technology, and this study tries to investigate cloud computing security concerns and potential solutions. A systematic review was conducted utilizing the databases Scopus, PubMed, Science Direct, and Web of Science. Firstly, this paper discussed the basics of cloud computing environment and mapped that how this technology can be helpful for health care sector. Technical, managerial, security and legal aspects while implementing cloud-based health care has also been observed and discussed. We have also discussed various cloud-based healthcare solutions offered by various companies such as Apple Health Kit, Google Health, AWS e-Health. Paper also presents the workflow of using cloud-based solution in health care sector.

articleTitle: Implementation of Convolutional Neural Networks on FPGA for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Object detection is a primary task in computer vision applications. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have emerged as potential technique and aggressively using in object detection and other computer vision applications. However convolutional neural networks (CNN) are more complex and higher computationally intensive and requires more hardware resources. To address this challenge, field programmable gate array (FPGA) offers significant advantages in terms of parallelism and hardware acceleration which makes them more suitable for accelerating CNN algorithms. This work implements a you-only-look-once (YOLO)v2 CNN on Xilinx zynq-7000 soc FPGA and the results show the increase in performance with reduced processing time and less power consumption compared to CPU based system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Area Efficient Parallel FIR Filters using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters are known for their stability and the reason being widely used over Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filters. Out of many FIR filters, parallel FIR filters are chosen the best over other filters in digital signal processing. This paper compares the design of a basic 3-parallel FIR filter as well as two versions of Area-Efficient 3-FIR filters. Booth’s algorithm and Carry-look-ahead adder are used as the basic components of this filter. The Area-Efficient filters are later compared after designing them. The simulation has been carried out using Xilinx ISE design suite 14.7. The FIR filters are later implemented on Spartan XC6SLX16-2FTG256 as the FPGA hardware.

articleTitle: Immersive Viewing of Dento-facial Medical Data in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) requires dynamic and responsive rendering technologies to offer an immersive user experience. Failing, users may experience motion sickness due to motion lag in virtual space. This work aims to create a framework with a higher framerate to decrease the motion sickness in turn increasing the virtual world viewing quality. Essentially, an interactive environment is developed between existing volume rendering engines OpenGL and GPU-based ray casting techniques for rendering the dentofacial data volume. The developed visualization methods are incorporated into Head Mount Device(HMD) to offer immersive effects. The performance of the VR rendering application measured in terms of framerate was observed to be 125 frames per second, significantly higher than the current HMDs framerate. In addition, the adaptation of rendered image quality is activated by adjusting the sampling distance and jitter to complete the rendering process in the allotted time. The achieved result is expected to offer satisfactory comfort to the viewer with reduced motion sickness, particularly in pre-surgical planning for dentofacial surgery.

articleTitle: FSD: A novel forged document dataset and baseline
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Forgery detection in multimedia is an emerging research area in the field of digital content security. The current research focuses on finding several solutions to digital image forgery detection but a small number of works have been reported for scanned document forgery detection. The reason would be the unavailability of a forged scanned document (FSD) dataset. A scanned document can be manipulated in different ways: deleting a region, copy paste a region of the document either in the same document or in another document. Detection of these manipulations becomes arduous when a post-processing operation is performed on the manipulated region. To advance research in this field, we created a large dataset for the FSD. To generate such a dataset, we collected scanned documents from the FUNSD dataset (Publicly Available). The resolution of each sample of the dataset is of size 755x1000. The samples of the dataset are forged using different post-processing operations. The dataset comprises 6656 instances of manipulated scanned documents with their ground truth masks. To build the baseline for forged scanned document detection, we evaluated state-of-the-art object segmentation algorithms on the FSD dataset. Experiments demonstrate that the FSD well represents forged scanned documents and is quite challenging.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Mongo DB: Features, Advantages, and Limitations
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mongo DB classified as NoSQL database which uses JSON-like documents to store data with optional schemas. Over the years Mongo DB has become more and more popular due to its easy to grasp user-friendly interface, scalability, and adaptability. This paper explains Mongo DB’s core characteristics, pros and cons. We will also discuss how to use Mongo Db efficiently and effectively and explore other popular use cases of this database.

articleTitle: An In-Depth Review of Blowfish Encryption Algorithm: Security, Performance, and Application
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The important components in the information protection is network securitywhich is reasonable for protecting all information which are passing through networked systems. Through this paper we comprehensively analyzes and survey the Blowfish, DES, AES, and other algorithms exploring its design principles, encryption process, security analysis, and practical implementations. It investigates the algorithm's strengths, weaknesses, and potential applications in contemporary cryptographic scenarios. Recent developments and alternatives in the field are discussed, offering insights into the algorithm's relevance and prospects. This review paper aims to provide researchers, practitioners, and cryptography enthusiasts with a thorough understanding of the Blowfish algorithm and its significance in the realm of symmetric-key cryptography.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Covid Chest X-Rays using a Game Theoretical Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project's goal is to develop a deep learning algorithm that is capable of correctly classifying images while making use of SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to provide explications for the model's predictions. The training of the model will be carried out on a dataset consisting of medical images, such as chest X-rays and MRI scans, which are commonly used for the purpose of diagnosing disease. The usage of SHAP values is meant to attribute the contribution of individual pixels within the input image to the output of the model, delivering significant insights into the process of prediction and the relative significance of distinct characteristics.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable X-Band Antenna with Notch Band Characteristics using EBG
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A fractal based inverted triangular shaped monopole antenna for X-band has been designed and reconfigured to reject narrow band frequencies from 8.90 GHz to 10.90 GHz. The antenna proposed has a peak gain ranging from 3.36 dBi to 6.18 dBi with an average peak gain of 4.95 dBi. Two double inverted C-shaped electromagnetic bandgaps (EBG) were symmetrically placed and implemented on the ground surface of the antenna to generate a notch frequency band. Two varactor diodes are integrated onto the EBG to reconfigure the notch frequency band electronically. Varactor diodes were tuned from 0.15 pF to 1.90 pF to reconfigure the notch frequency band from 8.90 GHz to 10.90 GHz. A comparative simulation and measured results of the fabricated model are analyzed and discussed. The size of the proposed antenna is 1.57λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> × 1.25λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> where, λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the guided wavelength at lowest cutoff frequency, 7.95 GHz.

articleTitle: Cloud Image Masking on Satellite Images Using U-Net Architecture of Deep Learning*
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Satellite photos are commonly utilized for many activities such as surveys, map creation, and surveillance, and cloud detection can make using such high-quality images easier. Global yearly mean cloud cover is roughly 66 percent, according to the International Satellite Cloud Climatology. Clouds frequently obscure surfaces and objects, making it harder to extract usable information from photographs. 38-Cloud [1] is the dataset that is utilized in this investigation. In order to segment clouds in satellite images, we used only three input channels from the dataset: Red, Green, Blur, and NIR (near infrared). This prompted us to take an entirely different strategy and create our own U-Net from the ground up and not use the vision libraries for preparing the dataset. The implemented U-Net model is showing 96.59% accuracy. This paper also includes the recent art of work carried out in the Cloud detection application.

articleTitle: ASL and Hand Gesture Emoji Translator Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: People with hearing loss communicate using a variety of sign languages, often using their hands. Regular people must learn these sign languages in order to interact with these individuals, which most do not do. As a result, the individuals with special needs may experience psychological and physical effects as a result. This project’s major goal is to address this problem and provide a simple means of communication for people with disabilities and their friends and family. However, in this world of digital people prefer social media platforms for communication and with that hand gesture emojis have gained significant popularity as a means of expressing emotions, actions, and ideas on digital platforms. These emojis, which depict a range of hand gestures, have been widely adopted due to their ability to convey nuanced meanings. Hand gesture emojis serve as visual representations of gestures commonly used in face-to-face communication, bridging the gap between physical gestures and digital interactions so this system can be used as ASL translator and also as emoji’s translator, this system requires only a laptop with an audio output and a camera to take live signs, process them, and compare them with the trained data to identify the perfect match and offer correct results. and it can also be upgraded to mobile application in the future. This solution is incredibly lightweight and has an accuracy rate of >96%.

articleTitle: Design of High Performance Adders Using Quantum Dot Cellular Automata (QCA)
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) is an advancing Nano electronic technology that promises to revolutionize the field of digital computing. QCA offers a fundamentally different approach to computing by exploiting the principles of quantum mechanics at the nanoscale level. This technology replaces traditional transistor-based circuits with small groups of quantum dots that can represent binary information using the spin of electrons. This paper provides an overview of the key concepts and principles of QCA, highlighting its potential advantages over conventional CMOS technology. This work proposes the ripple carry adder and carry lookahead adder designs using QCA and compare its performance with conventional CMOS designs. Finally, it is proved that QCA based adders have low power dissipation and high speed with respect to CMOS designs.

articleTitle: Open source image processing module to improve dental patient care in suburban and rural areas: Review Paper
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The study paper showcases a detailed study of dental imaging can be possible only under the technology of open-source image processing modules as it involves the use of the latest image processing tools and devices for improving both the quality and accuracy of dental images. Dental radiography delivers significant indications for medical diagnosis, treatment and superiority valuation. Many determinations have been prepared to mature numeral X-ray image investigation organizations to progress medical eminence. This paper has presented records, techniques, and consequences for assessing the superiority of dental caution-consuming circumferential dental radiographs occupied earlier and afterwards the technique. Dental experimental eminence assessment comprises many procedures, such as statistics of yearly dental appointments of kids and grownups of dissimilar eternities, different caries between kids with vigorous caries, endodontics to abstraction events etc. This eminence extent evaluates dental scientific superiority. At the macro level, It is needed to escalate the micro level equally well, such as thoughtful whether the treatment assumed to distinct teeth is operative or not. The original and developing ground in orthodonture is dental informatics, owing to its possibility to recover treatment and analysis, while exchangeable time and plummeting nervousness and exhaustion throughout the regular repetition. The usage of computer curriculums can comfort dental specialists in the creation of conclusions associated with deterrence, identification, as well as cure schedule, surrounded by others. This study paper will also discuss the efficiency of Image processing tools that help a dentist and dental professionals improve the treatment quality.

articleTitle: An Flexible Wearable Compact Metamaterial-loaded monopole Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this feild, the challenge is to construct a flexible antenna with good performance in the wearable environment. In this research work, a novel metamaterial loaded antenna is proposed to work in the wireless body area network. By employing a split ring resonator in the ground plane, we are able to obtain reduced size. The size of antenna is 25 mm x 19 mm x 0.3 mm with polyamide substrate making the antenna flexible. The obtained directivity in dB is 3.0529, with a good impedance matching. The proposed antenna is tested on cotton cloth textile material. In addition to this, the obtained specific absorption rate is 0.9 W/kg that is within the permissibe limits. No major difference is seen between the simulated and measured return loss. The return loss is tested with N9926A FieldFox Handheld Microwave Analyzer, 14 GHz. The simulated and measured return loss have been found in good agreement.

Author Keywords: metamaterial (Split Ring Resonator)wireless body area network miniturization

articleTitle: nn-morph: Simplifying deep neural network manipulation, transformation and analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, we describe a framework that permits a neural network model trained in Keras, to be modified by inserting custom layers or operation nodes before or after any existing node or layer. Pre-defined custom layer templates are made available for a user to customize as per their needs. Typical applications for such a framework include introspection of a network at runtime for instance to measure statistical parameters like max/min/variance of the activation tensors which can be used to design effective quantization schemes. Other applications include studying the impact of noise on the accuracy of the network, which can be useful for modeling non-idealities and determining end-to-end network performance on systems with resistive memory technologies like Phase Change Memory (PCM) where the weights stored in memory are susceptible to non-idealities from various sources like conductance drift.

articleTitle: Reconnaissance Robot for Military Operation and Multipurpose Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The escalating global threat of militancy poses a significant challenge to global security. In response, this paper proposes a wireless-controlled smart surveillance bot for military reconnaissance and multipurpose surveillance of an area. The 6-Wheel Drive (6WD) bot is designed to operate autonomously or manually, utilizing wireless technology for communication. The autonomous mode incorporates an Ultrasonic Sensor for obstacle detection and avoidance, along with a supervision algorithm for precise movement. The bot's multi-sensory capabilities enable it to detect enemy positions via camera and provide live streaming to authorized personnel during military raids. Additionally, it can identify movement, confirm human presence in hazardous areas, and observe real-time streaming of the surrounding environment. The system employs an Arduino for sensor and status data transmission to the Raspberry Pi via serial communication. The Raspberry Pi 4 handles video streaming and wireless command reception, enabling personnel to control the bot via a web page interface. The integration of a GPS module allows for location tracking during rescue operations. With the ability to switch seamlessly between autonomous and manual modes, authorized personnel can effectively adapt to circumstances and make informed decisions based on live streaming observations.

articleTitle: Bivariate polynomial key update based on interpolation for WSN
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In bivariate polynomial based key management schemes polynomial is fixed and it is secure upto t nodes. In polynomial key management schemes no polynomial update and key update.If no polynomial update and key update if t nodes are captured entire network will compromise. This problem addressed in this paper. The proposed approach uses t degree bivariate polynomial that is generated uniquely by each cluster head from their predeployed points. In each session, the base station sends a new polynomial associated point to the cluster head. After$\left({_2^{t + 2}}\right)$ sessions, the pairwise key is dynamically updated between pairs to avoid a node capture attack. Also, in each session, cluster heads generate a new random number to avoid a replay attack. Mutual authentication to avoid man in the middle attack. In results it takes less memory . Security analysis is verified in Scyther Tool.

articleTitle: Hash based image indexing framework using deep earning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have demonstrated their effectiveness in extracting discriminative features from images, allowing for accurate image recognition and classification. Traditional search approaches, on the other hand, become computationally expensive and impractical as image databases expand. This research presents a system for indexing CNN characteristics in order to enhance the efficiency of large-scale image search. The necessity to develop indexing frameworks capable of effectively extracting relevant photos from enormous datasets motivates this research. This framework contributes to the improvement of the performance of content-based image retrieval systems by establishing an efficient indexing framework for CNN features. The system draws on existing cutting-edge techniques to create an indexing framework capable of organizing and retrieving images based on similarities in the complex and multidimensional CNN feature space. To lower the computational cost and storage needs associated with large-scale picture searches, the system makes use of image features and hashing methods.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Undersampling and Oversampling Methods for Flood Forecasting in Bangladesh using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Catastrophic floods can inflict devastating destruction on human life, agricultural lands, buildings, and economies. Bangladesh is highly vulnerable to this natural calamity, with varying levels of destruction occurring year after year. Accurately predicting flood occurrence could save Bangladesh from this destruction, but due to imbalanced data, this is nearly impossible. Machine learning models become biased towards only one class because of imbalanced data, leading to incorrect predictions. To address this issue, we employed different undersampling and oversampling techniques for data balancing and then compared the effectiveness of these techniques for predicting flood occurrence in Bangladesh using various machine learning models. The results highlight the Random Forest Classifier with Random Oversampling as the most successful combination, achieving an accuracy rate of 97.62%, precision of 96.09%, recall of 99.34%, F1-score of 97.69%, and ROC score of 97.61%. Because of Random Forest Classifier’s ensemble learning ability, feature handling, and resistance to overfitting, it outperforms other techniques when paired with Random Oversampling to solve class imbalance.

articleTitle: Automated Traffic Monitoring Control for Improved Visibility On Curve Hilly Road Using Internet-of-Things
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Traffic management is a frequent problem these days due to the rapid growth of urban population. There are more accidents due to improper traffic management. Accidents happen frequently, especially in hilly areas, but people still don't care about safety when driving on roads. In addition to poor driving skills, terrain problems such as blind spots, increased number of U-turns, poor lighting (lack of streetlights), and lack of support equipment are the causes of accidents. Due to increased urbanization, population growth, the creation of varied living spaces, and the widespread distribution of vehicles, roads are in good condition and modernized, but there are still significant human casualties from accidents. In order to solve this problem, IoT-based traffic control system in mountainous area was developed. A screen can be set up at the curves and the sensors are placed on the roads. The design is implemented to control traffic in hilly areas using technologies available in the market and using IoT.

articleTitle: Stress Level and Emotion Detection via Video Analysis, and Chatbot Interventions for Emotional Distress
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Stress is a ubiquitous issue in modern culture that may have serious consequences for people's mental and physical health.In this study, we offer a unique method for detecting and relieving stress by using face data acquired via live video, texting via a chatbot utilising convolutional neural networks (CNN), and mood-based music suggestions via Spotify API. Our method combines the benefits of real-time facial feature capture via live video with the simplicity of messaging via a chatbot. We employ CNN to analyse facial expressions and extract stress-related characteristics. Using CNN, our chatbot converses with the user, offering advice and help to lower stress levels.The chatbot's stress detection model was built with VADER.Furthermore, we propose music depending on the user's mood as identified by live video, which can aid in relaxation and stress reduction.Our system can detect stress levels with an accuracy of 83.79% via face stress detection and 79.23% via chatbot, according to the results. The capacity of the chatbot to ease the user's tension is assessed using answer accuracy, which is 85.38%.Our suggested method has the potential to be a useful tool for individuals to monitor and control their stress levels, resulting in better overall health and well-being.

articleTitle: Self-Improved Beluga whale optimization algorithm based Optimal Trained Deep Maxout Model for Glaucoma Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Glaucoma is a fast-growing retinal disease, which is a chronic and neurodegenerative disease that affects patients progressively. The neuro-retinal nerve called the optic nerve, which connects the eye to the brain damages the eye due to lack of proper diagnosis. To diagnose this disease, ophthalmologists need to perform various tests. However, taking more tests requires a lot of time and that is expensive. Also, the early stage of glaucoma may not show any vision loss to the affected people. For detecting glaucoma, this paper intends to propose the glaucoma detection model that follows four phases including preprocessing, segmentation, Feature extraction, and glaucoma detection. In the Preprocessing phase, the retinal images are processed by median filtering. Subsequently, subjecting the preprocessed image to the segmentation, where the optic cup will be segmented by the improved U-net model. Subsequently, the features such as cup-to-disc ratio, inferior superior nasal temporal features, fractal features, and proposed Local Gabor features are derived from the segmented image. These extracted features are trained to the optimized DeepMaxout classifier for detection purposes. Finally, a novel self-improved Beluga whale optimization algorithm is proposed for the optimal training of DMN by tuning its optimal weights.

articleTitle: Cybernetic Technologies in Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The presently ongoing industry 4.0 is by far the most rapidly transformational and widely trending revolution as compared to its previous three technological generations. The fourth generation of industry deals with cybernetics, which includes smart automation, interconnectivity, machine learning, real-time data acquisition and control. The various cybernetic technologies active in this industry 4.0 consist of 3D printing, bigdata, artificial Intelligence, cyberphysical systems and more. These technologies are the reason behind the successful implementation of the fourth industrial generation practices. Cybernetic technologies help in real time monitoring, analysing and controlling physical industrial machinery, devices and objects through data collected through smart sensors connected to the internet-network cloud. Cybernetic technologies have a lot of daily applications including smart health monitoring, smart factory, smart home appliances, and so on. This paper presents some of the important aspects of cybernetc technologies in industry 4.0, including smart sensors, asset utilisation, product development, supply chain, predictive maintenance and more.

articleTitle: Tokenization effect on neural machine translation: an experimental investigation for English-Assamese
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Tokenization, as a research task, is mostly overlooked when dealing with machine translation as much emphasis is placed on modelling or data enhancement, not to speak for language pairs categorized as low-resourced. The current work takes up this task of an experimental analysis of tokenization on Neural Machine translation (NMT) on a resource-poor language pair: English-Assamese. Four implementations of tokenization available as library are selected for this study: Moses, Nltk, OpenNMT, IndicNLP. The efficiency of these tokenizers in handling the language specialities is also discussed. Both the source and target languages are tokenized with these methods and 12 different NMT models are developed by choosing different combinations of the tokenizers. Perturbations in the evaluation scores have been observed for each combination in both directions (En→As and As→En). It is striking to observe that tokenizing Assamese text with Moses produces the most degrading results. The tokenization effect is again confirmed by testing with the source text tokenized with different tokenizers wherein it was clear that the tokenization schemes followed during model training has to be adhered to produce the best results.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Enhancement of Ultra Dense Multiuser MIMO System by Using Wyner Model
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In modern wireless communication, energy consumption has emerged as a major problem for wireless network operators. With the advent of fifth generation (5G) wireless communication, energy efficiency (EE), one of key performance measurement indicators of wireless networks, has gained recognition. Multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) and cell densification are some of the most recent techniques that have proven to be highly effective in maximizing the EE of 5G wireless communications. Most of the research has been done on either MIMO or ultra-dense network (UDN), utilizing different precoding techniques. However, works that consider MU-MIMO, UDN, and precoding techniques jointly are rarely investigated. The cooperative design of UD MU-MIMO systems using the Wyner model, taking into account the power needs of the base station, user equipment, and the coverage area to increase the EE is the concern of this research. In this research, the optimal partial zero forcing (p-ZF) processing is used to deploy the combination of MU-MIMO and UDN with Wyner model. Numerical results show that the design consisting of the combination of MU-MIMO, UDN and precoding techniques (p-ZF) is more energy efficient compared to MU-MIMO with normalized p-ZF precoding.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Local Data Imbalance on Federated Learning Performance for IoT Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has experienced tremendous surge in the number of connected devices, resulting in an enormous amount of data being generated. Anomaly detection in such scenarios is crucial for ensuring the security and reliability of IoT systems. Federated Learning (FL) has been proposed as a viable solution for anomaly detection in IoT, allowing distributed devices to collaboratively learn a global model while keeping their data private. In this paper, we investigate the impact of local data imbalance on the performance of FL-based anomaly detection models in IoT scenarios. In general, data imbalance in FL can manifest either globally, where the collective data of clients is imbalanced, or locally, where the data of individual clients is imbalanced. To specifically examine the impact of the later, we use the X-IIoTID dataset and create three different data distributions, each consisting of 10 client devices.
