The aim of the project is to use image classification using a convolutional neural network (CNN), take a wheat leaf image as an input, and as a result, convey whether the leaf is healthy or not, if not, what disease it is having.

articleTitle: Target Detection Improvement in OFDM-IM JCR System using POGM
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an index modulated orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM-IM) based JCR system capable of generating target profiles with very high peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR). The modulation symbol cancellation method used in the conventional OFDM radar systems can be used only for the active subcarriers in the OFDM-IM systems resulting in partial channel information. The proposed JCR system recovers the full channel information without using modulation symbol cancellation and signal reconstruction; therefore, it is able to produce range-velocity profiles with high PSLR. Multi-target scenarios are considered in this paper, where the target detection and parameter estimation are carried out by using the proximal optimized gradient method (POGM), which is a sparse recovery algorithm. Simulation results show that the target parameters are estimated accurately, irrespective of the number of active subcarriers used in the OFDM-IM signal.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Interactive System for the Disabled Person
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Technology is focused on making life comfortable for humans nowadays. This comfort should be shared and enjoyed by a variety of people at large. The simple interfaces and interactive applications make various things easy and attractive for us. This technological advancement should not only aid general people, but it should also be focused on aiding a special group of people who may or may not be able to use various technological resources available. Thus, we propose this application called ‘Differences’ to celebrate the various groups of people and help ease their lives by providing necessary features to the people according to their specific needs.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fractional-Order Nonlinear PID Controller for Three-link Robotic Manipulator System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With more links, manipulator systems become substantially more effective and valuable, however at the expense of more complexity. In this study, the performance of a multi-input and multi-output highly rigid three-link robotic manipulator system (TLRMS) using a fractional-order nonlinear proportional, integral, and derivative (FONPID) controller for trajectory tracking along with X and Y positional movement are analyzed. The performance of the FONPID controller is carefully investigated and results are compared to the nonlinear proportional, integral, and derivative (NPID) as well as traditional proportional, integral, and derivative (PID) controllers. The cuckoo search algorithm (CSA) is used to optimize controller gains by choosing the minimum objective function criterion (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf>) which is the combination of the weighted sum of the integral of absolute error (IAE) and integral of absolute change in controller output (IACCO) values. The analysis's findings conclusively show that the FONPID controller performs better in trajectory tracking. This study advances fractional-order control techniques, especially when applied to sophisticated manipulator systems.

articleTitle: Integration of Power Gating with DTCMOS in the Design of MIMO filter
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The paper presents a new architecture for a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) filter based on current conveyors using Power Gating technology. And the configuration for design used is DTCMOS. The proposed architecture is aimed at improving the performance and reducing the power consumption of MIMO filters. The DTCMOS-based current conveyors are used to implement a transconductance amplifier and a transimpedance amplifier in the MIMO filter. The proposed architecture is simulated using a 45nm CMOS technology, and the results show that it achieves a significant improvement in the figure of merit (FOM) compared to conventional MIMO filters. Additionally, the proposed architecture has a reduced power consumption, making it suitable for low-power applications. Overall, the proposed architecture provides a promising solution for designing efficient MIMO filters.

articleTitle: Optimizing Sidelobe Levels in 5G Antenna Arrays: A Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm Approach for Enhanced Network Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The deployment of 5G networks requires advanced antenna technologies to meet the increasing demands for high-capacity and low-latency communication. Antenna arrays, known for their beamforming capabilities, are vital in achieving these goals. However, sidelobes in the antenna radiation pattern can introduce errors and significantly impact the system's overall performance. This paper proposes a novel beamforming optimization technique for linear antenna arrays (LLA) in 5G networks. Our approach leverages the power of metaheuristic algorithms, precisely the Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA), to optimize the array configuration and reduce the Sidelobe Levels (SLL). The main objective is to minimize the closest SLL to the main lobe, directly affecting antenna performance and frequency reuse. Simulations and statistical analysis are conducted to evaluate the performance of our proposed method. Comparative studies are carried out against well-known approaches, including Archimedes Optimization Algorithm (AOA), Chimp Optimization Algorithm (ChOA), and Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA), in terms of sidelobe reduction. The results demonstrate our proposed approach's superior performance and effectiveness in achieving lower SLL, which positively impacts the overall antenna performance and system efficiency. This research advances beamforming strategies in 5G networks by introducing a metaheuristic-based optimization approach for LAA. The findings provide valuable insights and guidance for designing high-performance antenna systems in next-generation wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Single Pixel Measurements through Fourier Phase Shifting in Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This article suggests a technique for improving images using Fourier single-pixel imaging (FSPI). FSPI is a computational imaging method that makes use of the Fourier transform to rebuild the picture after taking a number of measurements of a scene with a single detector. The proposed method investigates how the quality of the image that is reconstructed is impacted by sample pathways, SNR ratios, and phase shifts.In addition to exploring the best sampling pathways and SNR ratios that can improve image quality, the research compares the results obtained utilising three and four-phase shifts. The discussion of relevant work, the suggested approach, the findings of the experiments, and future study directions are included in the paper's conclusion. The suggested method generates high-quality images with a shorter data acquisition time and is practical for real-time imaging applications.

articleTitle: Testing of Real time Embedded Onboard Software : a Launch Vehicle Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The avionics system in safety critical aerospace systems plays an extremely important role in ensuring proper performance as well as safety of the mission. The Onboard Computer (OBC) that functions as the master in the avionics bus in launch vehicles is based on an indigenous processor. The development and testing of the Real Time Executive (RTE) software for the OBC, satisfying all requirements is a daunting task. This work describes the testing techniques employed for the RTE software in the reusable launch vehicle. Various dynamic testing techniques like unit testing, integration testing and system testing were employed to validate the OBC software. Validations were also carried out for the entire system utilizing different test beds, where all the subsystems are connected. In addition, the software was subjected to code inspection and rigorous reviews which constitutes static testing. The results of testing the onboard software are also elaborated. Subsequent to detailed analysis of all test results and incorporation of necessary corrections, the software was cleared for final flight use and its performance was normal in flight.

articleTitle: SLACOZE : Secure LoRa Ad-hoc Communication network Over the deadZonE
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wide Area Network (WAN) technologies, like cellular 4G and 5G, are well-known and enable data transmission over long distances. Cellular WAN consumes a lot of power, and it allows us to transmit large amounts of data at high speeds over long distances. High power usage is the cost of this trade-off. Because of that, it required a wireless network that uses very low power but covers a wider area than Wi-Fi. Solution for that is enter to the LoRa. Long-range is referred to as "LoRa". Semtech's LoRa technology is a pro-priority radio modulation that only addresses the physical layer of the stack. Low-power, long-distance transmission over the unlicensed ISM band is made possible by the Lora technology's usage of propriority Chirp Spread Spectrum modulation. The bit rate of LoRa transmissions is quite low. The speed is in the range of 10 kilobits per second. In this scenario, it maintains a secure communication with Low powering nodes in areas with no signal and to implement a system to recognize & notify the rest of the team, if they face to the abnormalities. Therefore, this whole system is a contribution of LoRa Key manager, Power control unit, Abnormalities tracking system & Location tracking system and the integration of several such devices creates a LoRa Ad-Hoc network. These kinds of projects are most important for teams who communicate inside a dead zone, like forest explorers, as well as for military terrain.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Detecting Psychological Instability: An Evaluation of Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: These days people all around the world put in a lot of effort to keep up with the rapidly growing world. Yet, as a result of this, every person has to cope with a variety of health problems, the most well-known of which is depression or stress, which can ultimately result in demise or other heinous actions. These irregularities can be referred to as psychological instability, which can be cured by pursuing some form of therapy advised by medical professionals. For this research, a dataset is taken from the internet and then data was processed using neural networks(NN) and few machine learning models were also used to check the accuracy whether the model is being more accurate and on the other hand an interface was created consisting a variety of questions which are related to the dataset that we are considering for this work and for the instability identification process we are using fuzzy techniques as the answers to these questions are created in that way and based on the answers received to questions output is determined about the level of instability that a person is having and based on that person can get the treatment required.

articleTitle: A framework for Interoperability in Blockchain Without Any Intermediaries
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This Blockchain technology has been growing for Information and Communication Technology (ICT) because of its features such as decentralized, peer to peer, secure, and immutability of data in the network. Due to enormous features of blockchain technology like immutability, tamper free and decentralised data storage, blockchain is gaining popularity day by day. Though there are divergent applications of blockchain but again due to lack of interoperation between different blockchains there is still a doubt of sustaianbility of blockchains for next decade.Interoperability between two or more blockchains is important for sharing exchanging and transfer of different data, assets and transactions from one blockchain to another blockchain to increase the scalability of blockchains as well as to increase the flesxible usage of blockchains in the security domain. Though there are few solutions available for interoperability, those limited to only for exchanges or for asset transfer but not for all the interoperability purposes together, such as transfer, share, exchanges all together, also they are using some intermediaries for all these type of interoperation. So in this paper we proposed a design of a framework for interoperability solution without any intermediaries; so that any blockchain can interoperate with each other without any external entity without compromising blockchain features

articleTitle: Mitigating Road Accidents in Hilly Regions: An Artificial Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The intent of this research is to develop a method for predicting traffic accidents in hilly areas by using a combination of Neural Networks and Genetic Algorithms. The model is built by looking at past data on road accidents and considering factors such as the weather, and other things that can affect the likelihood of an accident. By using this information, the Neural Network is trained to recognize patterns and then the Genetic Algorithm fine-tunes the Neural Network to improve the accuracy of the predictions. When compared to traditional methods, this new model is better at predicting accidents in hilly areas. This research could help local authorities implement targeted safety measures and prevent accidents from happening.

articleTitle: Optimizing Apache Kafka Deployments - Configuration customization is all you need
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Apache Kafka is an open source publish-subscribe message broker and distributed logging tool that has a widespread adoption in the modern world by companies like Uber, Airbnb, Linkedin and many more. Delivering extreme high volume event data to diverse consumers via a publish-subscribe messaging system with several out of the box optimizations on the 4 major pillars of latency, throughput, durability and availability makes this tool so much popular in the IT landscape. Kafka has the option to customize most of its configuration related parameters to optimize it the most for our use case. Some of the use cases have millions of writes per second, hence it needs to handle huge billions of volumes of data which cannot be done easily by a traditional database or key-value store pair. Some use cases like a chat application demands very low latency where storing the data can be delayed, but the recipient needs to get the sender’s message delivered as soon as possible. Some use cases like a banking application requires high durability over latency and throughput, where the data records must be stored in spite of any system failures. Latencies over 500ms can be tolerated but not data loss in any possible case. And finally some use cases like emergency systems, autonomous vehicles, these are some applications that have to be available for communication all the time and it really doesn’t demand low latency or high throughput or high durability.So the crux of this is, we should know to configure the application depending on our use case. In this paper we are comprehensively going to talk about how we can optimize Apache Kafka correctly depending on these 4 major pillars. After immense testing and brainstorming we have come up with a set of configuration parameters for each of these pillars which would provide a headstart to optimize the kafka deployment. Kafka’s ability to scale efficiently, but it can become a bottleneck if not properly configured. We have benchmarked the results along with those provided by Microsoft and Confluent. Instead of proposing, using graphs and metrics we imply it in a prudent way.

articleTitle: ADAPTER: Auto-Augmentation for Emotion Recognition in EEG - A Class and Subject Invariant Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Data Augmentation is essential to machine learning pipelines, particularly for developing robust models in emotion recognition tasks using EEG signals. The low signal-to-noise ratio of EEG signals and limitations on collecting large EEG datasets make data augmentation one of the easiest and most effective techniques for developing real-world emotion recognition models. It addresses class imbalance, distribution shifts, and lack of data, allowing the model to generalise and reduce overfitting. This paper introduces ADAPTER (Automatic Data Augmentation and PerTubation for Emotion Recognition), a novel automatic data augmentation strategy for emotion recognition using EEG signal classification. ADAPTER finds the best policy of geometric transformations across multiple classes in the classification dataset, such as SEED, without manually selecting from the pool of different transformations. It is tailored to be class and subject-invariant, ensuring that the resulting models are robust and generalisable across various tasks and subjects. The proposed technique outperforms the existing state-of-the-art model for SEED by 5% in terms of accuracy and 2% macro F1-score. ADAPTER showcases the potential of a flexible and adaptable data augmentation approach in enhancing the performance of EEG-based emotion recognition models while maintaining interoperability and control over the augmentation process.

articleTitle: Blockchain based Federated Deep Learning Framework for Malware Attacks Detection in IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Over the recent years, billions of IoT devices that do not have adequate security features have been created and deployed over internet, and with the increased bandwidth and lower latency of 5G networks these numbers expected to grow exponentially. Consequently, there is a pressing requirement of reliable methods to identify malware infected IoT devices present in a network. Traditional Centralized Deep Learning approach was used to train a model capable of detecting infected IoT devices, but this approach faces major challenges like data privacy violation, scalability and high network latency. A more efficient process Federated Deep Learning was proposed which aims to improve privacy and security by keeping data on the devices and transmitting only model parameters to a central location for aggregation and then this aggregated model reflected to the edge devices. Because of the centralized aggregation this approach is prone to adversarial attacks. To resolve these vulnerabilities, we presented a decentralized framework consisting of a chain of Federated blocks at each edge devices with cohere-consensus mechanism (FBCC). The framework makes use of blockchain technology both for updating local models and to store global models. We also came up with a novel cohere-consensus technique to facilitate the suggested FBCC, which efficiently cut down on the quantity of consensus computing while simultaneously lowering the risk of malicious attacks. At last, we conducted comprehensive testing of the frameworks with real-world datasets, in both benign and malicious environments. The results revealed that our proposed framework outperformed the other frameworks in the malicious environment, while demonstrating comparable efficiency in the benign environment. Additionally, we conducted a thorough comparison of the frameworks in terms of memory requirements and training time. FBCC framework, due to its core architecture, exhibited slightly lower performance than FDL. However, it maintained privacy as a top priority.

articleTitle: Analysis and study of IDSs for cybersecurity vulnerability detection and prevention: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Smart environments are worried about private keys and security problems. To prevent security attacks, which take benefit of a few of these intrusion detection systems (IDSs) and security vulnerabilities, were modeled. In the age of the Internet of Things (IoT), data generated by connected objects presents the fundamentals for big data analytics that could be used to recognize the anomalies and patterns in the data. Numerous cyber security systems use IDSs to detect intrusions that employ a variety of approaches and architectures. In this work, several research papers have been utilized based on diverse approaches used for detecting and preventing cyber security vulnerabilities. Moreover, this research work is reviewed by classifying them based on the detection approaches used in the preceding works. In addition, the research gaps and problems recognized in the previous works are stated; thus, the researchers can bring elucidation and improve their research in the future. The works in the literature are analyzed based on several features, such as performance evaluation measures, datasets utilized and approaches used.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Techniques based on Resource Provisioning in Cloud Computing: Compressive Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The era of cloud computing has arisen as a technology utilising the internet in the last few decades to realise the "utility" approach of technology for providing services with a high computational demand. The information technology and company resources, including as storage, networks, servers, and programmes, can be automatically allocated to cloud demands presented by individuals under the scenario of cloud computing. The trend towards virtualization technology used by the cloud computing infrastructure offers on-demand availability of system assets, including processing and storage. In cloud computing, emulation is used to distribute computing resources through an alternate communications network. The main goal of the scheduling is to reduce the requirement and impairment time and increase performance. In order to do a task successfully and precisely, scheduling is crucial. The present paper provides information on several work scheduling techniques utilised by researchers in the cloud computing environment. Therefore, it is open study to determine an approach by examining present challenges. The limitations. benefits, and prospects associated with various resource provisioning approaches are therefore addressed in the present research along with several methods developed for resource provisioning in cloud computing working with various scheduling algorithms.

articleTitle: Leveraging US Airport Performance to Propel India's Aviation Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The research study provides a comparative examination of selective international airports in the USA from 1988 to 2020, concentrating on their performance in terms of delays, infrastructure, and the number of flights served. The study uses publicly available data to identify patterns in each airport's operational performance and examine how each airport has changed over time. Over the years, each airport has encountered unique challenges and experienced a variety of triumphs, with some performing better than others in key areas. For instance, certain airports have made significant investments in technology and infrastructure, which have aided in reducing delays and enhancing the traveler experience. Others have struggled to meet the demand, which has resulted in crowding and higher wait times. This will help us to explore the key takeaways that may be drawn from how airports operate. The need of investing in infrastructure, technology, and personnel development in order to improve operational efficiency and customer satisfaction is emphasized. The insights of this research may be useful to stakeholders and policymakers in the Indian aviation sector, assisting them in understanding the difficulties airports face and creating solutions. Overall, this study represents a crucial step towards teaching India how to create a strong and sustainable aviation industry that would contribute to the economic development of the nation.

articleTitle: Segmentation of heart wall muscles and detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from 2D echo images using U- Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the development of an automatic technique to obtain the segmentation of the heart wall muscles from echo images using U-Nets. The detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and similar conditions is achieved by measuring the thickness of the posterior heart wall in the left ventricle. We measure the thickness of the segmented heart wall using repeated morphological operations in the form of erosion to give us an idea of its real thickness. Medical literature suggests that if the thickness of the heart wall is greater than 15mm, then we classify the image as a potential case of HCM. In our experiment, we have taken 139 images in our training, and 34 images in our test dataset in order to examine the accuracy of our technique. We find that the U-Net obtains an accuracy of 0.85 in terms of the Dice similarity coefficient.

articleTitle: Data Storage, collection, and Transmission in Smart Agriculture Using Bloom Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Population growth, climate change, and sustainable farming practices drive the demand for smart agriculture. To meet the projected 60% increase in food demand by 2050, efficient production and sustainable practices are crucial. Smart technologies like sensors and drones address climate change’s impact on agriculture by monitoring crops and adapting to changing conditions. However, smart agriculture generates vast amounts of data that traditional methods struggle to handle. As probabilistic data structures, Bloom filters offer efficient solutions for data management by enabling quick identification and retrieval without extensive computational resources. They are particularly useful in crop disease detection, aiding prompt management and prevention. Scalable Bloom Filters (SBF) address limitations like false positives and dataset size by dynamically expanding the filter as the dataset grows. SBF improves efficiency, reliability, data security, and transmission by limiting access to authorized nodes, reducing congestion and costs. Using SBF in smart agriculture makes the data storage, collection, and transmission process less time-consuming, space efficient, and with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Review of Image Super Resolution for Low Light Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image Super Resolution is the enhancement of a low resolution image to obtain its high resolution counterpart. It is an important technique in computer vision and has many practical use cases such as medical imaging and surveillance. In this paper, we study the usefulness of applying Image Super Resolution for Low light image enhancement. While a lot of research has already been done in low light image enhancement, most of the methods proposed so far introduce artifacts in the images and fail to produce finer details due to the limited amount of data they are trained on. In this paper, we review and analyze state-of-the-art super resolution methods to enhance the results from low light enhancement models. To this end, we first provide a taxonomy of methods, datasets, and metrics for Super Resolution. Finally, we experiment with different combinations of Low Light Image enhancement methods and Super Resolution methods to establish the effectiveness of using the latter in low light enhancement and show that it produces visually better results.

articleTitle: Monkeypox Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The monkeypox virus is gradually reemerging as COVID-19 viral infections decline globally. The recent outbreak in the early 2022 had grown fear and concern in people, making them believe that it would spread like COVID-19. Public health organizations struggled to contain the present outbreak as healthcare professionals from all over the world tried to become familiar with the many clinical signs and treatment of this infection. Early identification is, therefore, a crucial step to stop them from spreading broadly throughout society. AI-based detection may be able to locate them at an early stage. Such detection and prediction techniques have brought about optimistic outcomes. It also implies that the proposed approach is appropriate for mass screening by health practitioners. In image processing-based diagnostics, such as detection of cancel, identification of tumor cell, and COVID-19 patient detection, machine learning has lately demonstrated great promise. Therefore, as monkeypox spreads to human skin, a similar technique might be used to detect it. To help with the condition's subsequent diagnosis, a picture can be obtained and a dataset containing similar images of the infection can be utilized to develop a near-exact prediction model. In this review, we discuss the clinical diagnosis, management, and improvement of the classification accuracy of monkeypox images for development of prediction models using ML. We also discuss the historical and contemporary outbreaks of the monkeypox virus. This study is being conducted in light of the ongoing epidemics in various parts of the world.

articleTitle: Web (Network) Traffic Time Series Forecasting and Resource Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Businesses that depend on their websites to produce leads, conversions, and money must be able to accurately forecast future website traffic. Accurate traffic forecasting depends heavily on statistical and machine learning methods, particularly time series forecasting. Invaluable trends and patterns can be found by examining previous website traffic data, which then helps the creation of predictive models. Building forecast models using techniques such as ARIMA, Prophet, and LSTM RNN is a widespread practise. Popular computer languages like Python and R are often utilised. For the purpose of predicting future online traffic numbers, these models are trained on historical data. Usual measures for assessing model accuracy include the root mean square (RMS) value. The RMS value for the LSTM RNN model is normally about 20.8, whereas the ARIMA model captures data around 511. These metrics are expressed graphically in addition to numerically to make visualisation and analysis easier. Organisations and website owners may properly plan their marketing and advertising campaigns and make wise investment choices to enhance the performance of their websites with the help of accurate website traffic forecasts.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model for Heart Disease Prediction Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Heart disease poses a significant global health threat, being one of the leading causes of death. Accurately predicting cardiac disease is essential for effective prevention and treatment. In this study, we offer a technique based on deep learning for predicting heart disease that outperforms several other machine learning models which includes logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, Gaussian naive Bayes, and multi-layer perceptron. Our model architecture comprises multiple layers of 1D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with a max pooling layer applied after every two 1D convolutional neural network layers. Following these layers, we incorporate a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layer and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer. Additionally, the model includes two dense layers with softmax activation. To mitigate overfitting, we employ regularization techniques such as batch normalization and kernel regularization. For training and evaluation, we utilize the Cleveland dataset, which consists of 303 samples and 14 features encompassing patient demographics, medical history, and laboratory test results. Prior to training, we preprocess the data and perform normalization using standard scalar. Our model achieves an impressive accuracy of 93.3% in predicting heart disease, which demonstrates the effectiveness of deep learning for this task. This result highlights the potential of utilizing advanced techniques in cardiac disease prediction to enhance healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Spectrum predictions for Cognitive Healthcare system
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The prevailing pandemic scenario and the constant explosion of wireless devices lead to demand for a large spectrum. There is a crucial need for regular supervision of patient's health in these dire situations of a pandemic. This demands a smart solution for healthcare based on the latest technologies. This research work presents a detailed review of the latest advancements in the context of smart healthcare and medical imaging. This research work also proposes a novel framework for Cognitive healthcare based on Deep Learning. A unique spectrum prediction model has been proposed that combines the Grey model and Long Short Term Memory functionalities and allocates spectrum to the patients according to their risk classification (high, medium, and low). This research work describes the distinct novel applications of Cognitive radio, Deep learning, and the Internet of things in the Smart healthcare and Medical Imaging context. The proposed LSTM-Grey model has also been compared with existing spectrum sensing methodologies based on LSTM and CNN. All simulation results based on detection probability, false alarm probability and Accuracy of prediction indicate that LSTM-Grey model outperforms the existing solutions for healthcare system. The unique solution proposed based on the Grey model and LSTM for spectrum prediction enables transmission of medical data on free spectrum slots for real-time supervision of patient's health. The Deep Learning-based Cognitive Healthcare system is a promising candidate for Smart Healthcare supporting swift diagnosis, tracking, and patient health supervision.

articleTitle: Explanatory Case Study: Digital Forensics Investigation on DJI Spark Drone
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Drones are now widely used and have grown in popularity in recent years. However, as a result of their greater use, there have been more crimes involving drones. In this explanatory case study, digital forensics methods are used to analyze a DJI Spark drone discovered at a crime scene. The purpose of this inquiry is to obtain vital data that might help with the investigation of drone-related crimes. The drone’s memory card and remote controller, which have flight records, pictures, and videos on them, have important details about the crime and how the drone was used. We gather and examine this material using digital forensics techniques. Investigative personnel will then be able to recognize potential suspects and comprehend the drone’s participation in the crime. Important details, such as the drone’s flight path, the location of the murder scene, and the identities of the people involved, are revealed by the recovered data. This explanatory case study emphasizes the importance of digital forensics in the analysis of drone-related crimes. Drones will probably be employed more frequently in criminal acts as they become more prevalent in society. Investigators may keep ahead of the curve and efficiently use drones as a source of priceless evidence in criminal investigations by using competent digital forensics techniques.

articleTitle: An NFNet-Based Approach for Enhanced Bearing Fault Classification Using Vibrational Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The present work proposes a novel approach for detecting bearing faults in induction motors using vibrational signals. The proposed method employs a Normalizer-Free ResNet (NFNet) architecture to extract relevant features from 2D image representations of raw vibration data and a classification model to identify the presence of a fault. We convert the vibrational signals into 2D images by applying the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) technique, which offers a time-frequency analysis of the signals. The proposed method improves accuracy over conventional approaches along with reduced computational overhead by using high-performance NFNet architecture for classification. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS) datasets of vibration signals from induction motors, experiencing various bearing faults. The results indicate that the suggested framework outperforms the existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art results. This method can be used for real-time monitoring of induction motors to detect bearing faults and prevent potential equipment failures, making it highly useful for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Multilingual and Mixed-lingual Digit Speech Recognition System for Indian Context
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Voice assistants, customer service center automation, and voice-controlled devices all rely heavily on digit speech recognition. For multilingual countries like India, Canada, and Belgium to communicate in more than one language, there is a need for multilingual and mixed-lingual digit speech recognition (DSR) systems. This is the main emphasis of the proposed work. An extensive database of digit utterances from 0 to 9 for various Indian languages of Telugu, Kannada, Hindi & Tamil are self-recorded and used for the experimental work. Following the initial preprocessing by noise elimination from the self-recorded samples, spectrographic characteristics were extracted, and finally, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is applied for classification to identify the digits. The proposed multilingual DSR model resulted in an accuracy of range 89% to 96% and a loss value between 0.144 to 0.878 varying for each language whereas the mixed-lingual DSR model resulted in an accuracy of 92% and a loss value of 0.615.

articleTitle: BSeVS – A Smart e-Voting System based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Security and privacy has always been a major concern for wider adoption of electronic voting systems since the election results have both major economic and political influences all around the world. The challenges of an e-voting system like anonymity, secrecy, verifiability and authenticity is yet to be fixed and can be resolved by utilizing the Blockchain technology. Blockchain technology can improve voting process security, transparency, immutability, and dependability. Blockchain is a distributed, digital, consensus-based system for securely storing information. In this paper, a Blockchain based Smart e-Voting System (BSeVS) is implemented, which is utilizing the Hash functions and Elliptic Curve Cryptography to resolve the issues of the e-voting scheme. It enhances the end to end safety of e-voting mechanism without compromising the integrity and authenticity of voting environment. The results show that the BSeVS is performing better than existing voting schemes in terms of security and time complexity.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Personal Identifiable Information (PII) Label Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today's data-driven world, the protection of PII is of paramount importance to safeguard personal privacy. PII tags serve as crucial markers for identifying and processing sensitive information within databases. However, the authentication and registration of PII tags can be time-consuming and error prone. To address this challenge, we propose a method for privacy controlled PII tag detection that harnesses the power of machine learning (ML) combined with regular expressions. Proposed approach leverages various techniques, including feature engineering, adaptive learning, and machine learning, to extract meaningful patterns and relationships from data. By training the model on large datasets that encompass diverse PII elements such as names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and social security numbers, enable it to learn and classify PII identifiers across different documents effectively. One of the key advantages of the proposed method is its ability to automate the detection of PII identifiers, thereby reducing the reliance on manual interpretation and minimizing the potential for human error. By integrating machine learning algorithms, empower organizations to efficiently identify and process sensitive information present in their databases, bolstering privacy protection measures. Moreover, this approach facilitates the development of scalable and accurate solutions for privacy based PII tag search. This advancement paves the way for enhanced data privacy across the enterprise, ensuring compliance with regulations and standards pertaining to the protection of personal information. By combining the strengths of ML and regular expressions, the proposed method enables organizations to detect and handle PII identifiers more effectively. This not only streamlines data management processes but also strengthens privacy safeguards, and more secure and privacy-aware data ecosystem.

articleTitle: Automation Intervention for Monitoring Agriculture Farming Scale: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Agricultural data is only valuable when it has been managed successfully. As data has evolved into the fundamental ingredient in contemporary agriculture to assist farmers with vital decision, latest developments in managing data are causing Smart Agriculture to rise dramatically. With factual information obtained by sensors, significant advantages emerge with the goal of enhancing production and ecology. This type of data-driven farm management is built on information that can boost efficiency by preventing resource waste and contamination of the ecosystem. Data-driven farming, with the assistance of automated solutions using artificial intelligence techniques, lays the groundwork for potential sustainable farming.This article analyses the current state of sophisticated agricultural systems by rehashing each critical step, from data processing in field crops to variable interest rate implementations, so that farmers can make optimised decision making to save funds while safeguarding the natural environment and converting how meal would be generated to meet the upcoming population explosion.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wireless Charging Schedules in Sensor Networks: A Hybrid GSA-SA Approach for On-Demand Mobile Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Prior work on Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) has found that Sensor Node (SN) low energy capacity limits their ongoing operation. Recent discoveries in the field of Wireless Energy Transfer (WET) technology has emerged as a viable solution to sensor nodes’ low energy capacity. It creates dependable Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks (WRSNs). Recently, there has been a lot of interest in including Wireless Mobile Chargers (WMCs) in WRSNs to refill the energy of key sensor nodes (SNs) through WET. The basic concept of WET is the use of one or more (WMCs) to recharge SNs, resulting in the development of (WRSNs). In on-demand WRSN, optimize the order in which the SNs are charged (i.e., the charging schedule). Furthermore, when creating a WMC's charging schedule, we need to consider that requesting SNs creates both space and time constraints by considering these parameters. In this paper, we propose a hybrid Gravitational Search Algorithm-Simulated Annealing (GSA-SA) based recharge schedule for replenishing the sensor nodes which can be used to optimize sensor node deployment to maximize network coverage, reduce energy usage, and increase network lifespan. Our solution includes a unique strategy for efficient fitness functions. We do extensive simulations on the proposed system to show how it outperforms novel algorithms like First Come, First Served (FCFS), Nearest Job Next with Preemption (NJNP), and Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA). In terms of charging latency.

articleTitle: Disaster Assistance Intelligent Agent
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Virtual characters are controlled by artificial intelligence in video games and movies. Controlling these characters when they are surrounded by people is known as crowd simulation. In this work, we propose to employ intelligent agents and decision trees to simulate a realistic scenario in which our agent will lead the human behavioural AI and identify the best route to the goal or the best circumstances to the objective avoiding all the obstacles in the path. This crowd simulation will be used to make intelligent agents which can find the best path during the situation of any disaster and show humans the safest path which the humans can follow to get to the nearest safe points. Multiagent simulation, commonly referred to as a Crowd and Agent Simulation, is an approach used to simulate many people, animals or other characters interacting with each other in one place. These actors are expected to pursue their objectives, engage in the environment and coordinate with each other. It is expected that the simulated actors will pursue their goals, interact with the environment, and communicate among themselves. Crowd simulations find utility in various areas, including the enhancement of training environments and virtual worlds, the optimization of architectural planning, and the refinement of AI-driven characters' driving behaviors in video games and movies.

articleTitle: NetMiner: Identifying Failure-Inducing Patterns in the Logs Generated by Network Monitoring Software
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To ensure uninterrupted network communication among multiple sources, the network administrator needs to do real-time monitoring of network logs. Due to its huge volume and streaming nature, it is almost impossible to do a manual analysis of the logs generated by different network monitoring software. Moreover, these logs may contain a limited amount of data regarding the identity, location, capacity, etc. of a user due to privacy issues. Therefore, we propose an automated system named NetMiner for performing log analysis that requires only insensitive data such as the network’s current status and messages related to that status. We collect recent 30 days logs using the network monitoring tool PRTG (Paessler Router Traffic Grapher) and perform data analysis by leveraging a data mining technique called Fpmax. Our proposed technique NetMiner can identify patterns that may lead to failure and warn the network administrator about upcoming failures. Our experimental results show that NetMiner is both effective and efficient in identifying failure-inducing patterns in logs generated by network monitoring software.

articleTitle: Identification of Distributed Denial of Service Attacks Employing L-BFGS Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Internet speed and capacity are crucial components of any communication technology in the modern era. Customers should expect excellent speed and a lot of bandwidth. A DDoS (Distributed denial of service) assault, which is a well-known attack, is the biggest threat in communication. DDoS attacks limit the user’s speed and bandwidth. In order to produce this work, we used the updated dataset, CICDDoS2019, and undertook tests using a variety of machine learning methods. We investigated which features had the strongest relationships with the analysis’s projected classes. This research proposal offers a machine learning-based L-BFGS (Limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno) algorithm-based DDoS assault detection method. An HPC Python platform was used to carry out the simulation and experiment for the suggested research project. The accuracy, true and false negatives, along with true and false positives, confusion matrix structures, and other outcome measures are all evaluated in this study. The proposed method shows better results as compared to other previous methods. Index Terms—DDoS attack, MLP Classifier, LBFGS, Machine Learning.

articleTitle: Advancing Address Standardization through NER with BERT
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The address is a critical data point utilized in various industries, including E-commerce, Banking, Insurance, and Delivery. Address standardization is essential for maintaining good data hygiene, enabling companies to validate the information and ensure accurate parcel delivery in real-time and over the long term. This work investigates the use of named entity recognition (NER) for standardisation.NER categorizes text into entities such as name, address, organization, state, location, and more, making it a valuable tool for identifying various parameters and drawing conclusions for various projects. The study considers the implementation of various tagging techniques to make the process more accessible. The software developed finds extensive use in fraud detection, machine translation, and information retrieval. NLP also plays a crucial role in NER, with several applications, including text identification, machine translation, and lexicon text recognition. The study presents an innovative approach to address standardisation using NER and demonstrates its effectiveness in improving data hygiene and accuracy.

articleTitle: A Robust Edge Detector In The Presence Of Impulse Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Edge detection is a challenging task with many applications in image processing. Edge detection in images can be accomplished using various methods and well-known operators. The effectiveness of these techniques is frequently influenced by the extent of image detail preserved and the application at hand. Edge detection amplifies the noise, which has a major impact on their structural features. Impulse noise, often known as salt-and-pepper noise, is one such type of noise that affects the quality of images. Smoothing filters are frequently used to eliminate this kind of noise from images in order to reduce the noise's variation and maintain the image quality. The study presents a novel technique for detecting edges in images that utilizes denoising methods to retain image details while preventing blurring and preserving sharp edges along boundaries, even when high impulse noise is present. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated by measuring its performance using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), and is compared to the commonly used CANNY Edge detector.

articleTitle: An IoT Based Arduino - Nano Driven Smart Shopping Cart
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A shopping center or supermarket is a location where a variety of items are offered in one location, which has in fact made our lives simpler and more convenient. However, the process of standing in long queues at the bill counters to get the products billed and to make the payment is very time consuming and frustrating. Online shopping is now very attractive to people because of the wide variety and low cost of purchasing, but also quickly compare to offline shopping. In that situation we provide smartness in shopping and payment of bill that alone can make people look back to shopping centers and supermarkets for offline shopping. Therefore, we introduce an IoT-based Arduino Nano smart shopping cart with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID-sensors), and a Wi-Fi module can be utilized as an alternative to the bar code scanning procedure to solve this issue. The RFID tags or stickers which are attached to the products will be scanned by the RFID sensors present on the cart and the information about the product like price, quantity and name will be seen on the LCD screen of the cart in addition gets stored in the mobile application of the customer. The entire purchase information will be sent to the shop owner’s server wirelessly by using Wi-Fi module. Finally the bill payment will be done by any UPI-ID in smart way. This smart shopping cart eliminates the need for a billing counter, reduces time and creates a convenient shopping experience for a customer.

articleTitle: A Transfer Learning Approach with MobileNetV2 for Parkinson’s Disease Detection using Hand-Drawings
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease is a condition that affects common human movements because of the brain’s failing neurons. The primary cause of this disease is a deficiency of dopamine in the brain, which can also cause changes in blood pressure, eating difficulties, and disrupted sleep. For patients to receive proper treatment and to improve their health, it is essential to detect Parkinson’s disease at an early stage, as there is currently no cure for the disease. To address this, our research focuses on using spiral and wave hand-drawings as a means of early detection. We developed a modified MobileNetV2 approach with deep learning to accurately predict Parkinson’s disease using these drawings. Our approach achieved a high accuracy of 97.70%, with a low error rate of 2.30%, while using fewer parameters than other models. Our findings suggest that using hand-drawings as a diagnostic tool can greatly improve the accuracy of Parkinson’s disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Agricultural Expertise: A Federated Learning-CNN Approach for Potato Leaf Disease Multi-Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study uses a CNN in a federated learning environment to categorise and separate several illnesses that affect potato leaves. The primary focus is on the agricultural sector and the significant role of federated learning in diagnosing potato leaf illnesses. The growing need for machine learning approaches that provide adequate privacy protection makes this research more critical. Three data sets supplied by numerous customers served as the basis for training the federated learning model. Five different disease kinds and a healthy leaf state were included in the six categories that made up these data sets. The results showed that all three consumers, with accuracy levels ranging from 85.75% to 93.60%, had exceptional levels. The F1 score fluctuated between 87.46% and 90.89%, while recall rates ranged from 83.33% to 92.54%. Surprisingly, the model kept its accuracy between 96 and 98 per cent. It was possible to acquire a macro average of 90.00% accuracy, 89.52% recall, and 89.41% F1 score by combining the learning from all three client models. The F1-score was 89.40%, the accuracy was 90.08%, and the recall was 89.47% according to the weighted average measures. Precision, recall, and F1-score micro averages were 90.07%, 89.44%, and 89.38%, respectively. This study shows that federated learning has the potential to be a very accurate method for identifying illnesses in potato leaves while protecting the privacy and handling dispersed agricultural data. The findings also suggest that this approach could have broader applications for distributed agricultural data analysis on a larger scale, inviting further research into its utility across a more diverse range of crops and diseases.

articleTitle: Malicious Traffic Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: While the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to see tremendous expansion around the globe, its security continues to lag far behind. IoT devices were the focus of more than thirty percent of all mobile network spam that were discovered. The use of Neural Networks for the detection of malicious traffic on these often-unattended devices has shown encouraging results. This project is primarily aimed to create an automated system for classification of malicious traffic in an IoT network. In this process, the first step is to prepare/collect a proper dataset for the specific task. The CIC IoT Dataset was used in this instance. The second step includes the preprocessing of the data. In the third step, in order to visualize the files, the files are converted into images using a binary visualizer that is capable of converting any binary file into a colored image. After visualizing the images, the final dataset is prepared. In the fourth step, a Convolutional Neural Network is created and the dataset is fed to the neural network model with 90% training size, 10% validation size of the dataset. During training the model, a 99.9% of training, 99.8% of validation and 81% testing accuracy is obtained. The training loss is reduced to 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> and validation loss is reduced to 1.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>.

articleTitle: Does Sri Lanka Have a Good Maritime Strategy to Stop Cyber-Terrorist Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Maritime cyber-terrorist attacks have become a major concern to the entire world in recent decades. Everyone should be more aware of marine strategies to prevent cyberterrorist attacks, both locally and globally. This study investigates how Sri Lanka and the Sri Lanka Navy (SLN) may successfully address maritime security concerns by utilizing current resources and developing a marine strategy to counter such maritime cyber-terrorism assaults. The literature review in this thesis primarily evaluates the level of understanding in Sri Lanka concerning when marine cyber terrorism strikes may occur. Furthermore, this thesis investigates if Sri Lanka has any maritime rules and regulations. The use of such laws and regulations will concentrate on how they can increase their expertise.

articleTitle: Classification Of Carnatic Music Ragas Using RNN Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Present-day listeners can find it challenging to invest the time and effort necessary to learn the fundamentals of a particular genre of music. It would be easier to study Carnatic music in a shorter length of time if a paradigm that classifies the ragas existed. This would appeal to a bigger number of people since it would take less time to learn Carnatic music. In this sort of exploratory study, audio recordings are utilized as input to construct a model that can categorize classical music into a range of ragas. The model can also classify different types of classical music. For this, the features are retrieved by employing signal processing techniques to extract MFCCs, Spectral Rolloff, Zero Crossing rate, Spectrograms, and Spectral Centroids. After that, RNN Deep Learning models viz. LSTM and Bidirectional LSTM were trained and assessed to evaluate the model performance. The evaluation accuracy of these models came out to be 92.13% and 97.63% respectively.

articleTitle: Real-time Hand Gesture Recognition Using MediaPipe and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Hand gestures are an important form of communication, especially for individuals who use American Sign Language (ASL) to communicate. This study explored the use of Hand Gesture Recognition (HGR) using a dataset of 135,000 images, with 27 classes representing the letters A to Z and the space character. The MediaPipe framework and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with four hidden layers were used for building a gesture recognition system. Also to prevent overfitting, two dropout layers. In the input and hidden layers, the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function was utilized, and the softmax function was used in the output layer to predict probabilities for each class and obtained an accuracy of 99.34%, indicating the effectiveness of this approach for HGR. This study has important implications for improving communication for individuals who use ASL and may lead to the development of more advanced gesture recognition systems which will be beneficial to those who are deaf or dumb.

articleTitle: Access Control and Encryption Techniques during Big Data Accessing Stage
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Privacy issues and data security are made worse by Big Data's velocity, volume, and variety. Being able to extract information from enormous amounts of data has gained relevance. The amount of data being produced is large. The key drivers of ongoing growth include the Internet's rapid spread, the Internet of Things (IoT), and another innovation. Since data generated by systems reflects the environment it was obtained from, user can use the data that acquire from them to comprehend how they function. When it comes to cybersecurity, where the primary objective is to protect assets, this has grown in importance. This paper will look at current big data and cybersecurity studies. We will focus on one of the crucial data security tactics, namely access control and encryption techniques, by highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of conventional techniques and providing a set of requirements that any access control solution for Big Data platforms may satisfy.

articleTitle: DelNet based Systolic Peak Delineation in Remote PPG Signal from Facial Video Frames
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) technology has gained popularity in a short span of time due to its potential applications in cardiac health assessment. The existing studies have been accomplished under certain environmental constraints and focuses only on accurate heart rate (HR) estimation. The aim of this research work is to utilise a deep neural network (DNN) for the estimation of a reliable rPPG waveform with correct systolic peak localization. We propose a delineating network (DelNet) that is designed without any constraints. The rPPG waveform estimated from the network may be used to measure other cardiac parameters along with the HR value. The method is tested and validated on publicly available UBFC-rPPG dataset and also, compared with state-of-the-art approaches. The method is evaluated by comparing the derived HR and HRV parameters from the estimated rPPG waveform with the corresponding parameters measured from the ground truth PPG signal. For averaged HR, mean absolute error 1.132, root mean square error 1.448, standard deviation of error 0.927, and correlation coefficient 0.994 are found. Similarly, the resulted parameters of HRV analysis on estimated rPPG and PPG exhibit insignificant error values. The performance results show the effectiveness of the proposed scheme and its capability for cardiac healthcare system.

articleTitle: Automated speed breaker system using IoVT generated data for Electric Vehicle using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The identification of speed breakers on roads is crucial for ensuring a safe and comfortable driving experience for motorists. In this paper, we present an approach to identify speed breakers using Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques. The proposed approach is based on processing images captured by cameras mounted on vehicles or drones, which are commonly used for traffic monitoring and surveillance. The approach involves several steps, including image preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification. In the preprocessing step, images are enhanced to improve the quality and clarity of the speed breaker features. Feature extraction is performed using computer vision algorithms to extract relevant features such as shape, size, and color of the speed breakers. Finally, a classification model is trained using machine learning algorithms to classify the extracted features as speed breakers or non-speed breakers. To evaluate the performance of the proposed approach, we conducted experiments using a dataset of images collected from different roads. The results show that our approach achieved high accuracy and precision in identifying speed breakers, with an overall accuracy of over 90%. The proposed approach has potential applications in traffic management and road safety. By identifying speed breakers accurately and efficiently, road authorities can take appropriate measures to maintain the road infrastructure, improve driving conditions, and reduce accidents. Furthermore, the approach can be extended to identify other road features such as potholes, pedestrian crossings, and traffic signals, which can further improve road safety and traffic management.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach to Enhance IDS Accuracy using Hybrid LSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this research, the focus is on safeguarding networks and sensitive data from cyber threats. The study utilizes the UNSW-NB15 dataset to test the effectiveness of machine learning models, specifically BiLSTM models, in creating a reliable intrusion detection system. The dataset provides a more up-to-date and accurate representation of modern cyber attacks. The BiLSTM model, which considers both forward and backward dependencies in sequential data, is employed for detecting and classifying intrusions. The experimental results indicate a promising accuracy of 96.7%, as evaluated using accuracy, recall, and F1-score assessment criteria. This study contributes to the field of intrusion detection by highlighting the potential of deep learning techniques, particularly BiLSTM models, in achieving high accuracy and reliability, thereby enhancing network security and protecting sensitive information.

articleTitle: Computer vision approach for motion blur image restoration system
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a method for removing motion blur using the Inception ResNetv2 architecture. The proposed method combines Laplacian-variance-based classification with Inception ResNetv2 model tuning to achieve excellent inaccuracy. First, the Laplacian variance of the image is calculated, and based on this value, the image is classified into high, medium or low blur categories using quartile classification. The Inception ResNetv2 model is then tuned using hyperparameters to produce a blurred image. The proposed method is assessed using reference materials and compared to cutting-edge methods. Our results shows that it executes well with an average PSNR of 39.84. The proposed method also shows the better visual quality of out-of-focus images with more accurate, detailed edges and textures. The proposed method provides a reliable and efficient solution to eliminate motion inaccuracy. The combination of Laplacian-variance-based classification and Inception ResNetv2 model tuning provides a robust and efficient framework for motion blur removal with promising results that can be applied to different image processing applications

articleTitle: Ensemble Integration of Deep Learning Models for Gender-Based Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) holds significant importance in numerous applications, as it heavily relies on the precise extraction of acoustic information from speech signals. However, recognizing emotions within a complete utterance often poses challenges due to inherent ambiguity and varying probabilities assosiated with different emotions. Previous approaches have failed to account the acoustic variances between male and female speakers by employing combined dataset. Furthermore, relying on a single model can lead to limitations such as reduced robustness, overfitting, and limited generalization. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes an ensemble model that combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Residual CNN (RCNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures and utilizes features, extracted using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) on a gender-differentiated dataset that provides comprehensive and robust approach to speech emotion recognition. This proposed ensemble model is trained and evaluated on RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SAVEE and TESS datasets, resulting in weighted mean accuracy of 95.54%. The obtained results clearly indicate that the utilization of the Ensemble model instead of individual models improved the accuracy. The Ensemble model effectively encompasses diverse aspects of the data by leveraging the unique strengths of each model.

articleTitle: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Cyberbullying and Cyberhate Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cyberbullying and Cyberhate are significantly intensified with a rise in social media users. Rude and derogatory terminology is prevalent on social media, attacking individuals or communities. Bullying and hate are challenging to identify due to their appearance as sarcasm or implicit hatred. Various Artificial intelligence-inspired models are being deployed to curb and recognize widespread cyberbullying and hate. This study provides a detailed analysis of the role of AI in detecting Cyberbullying and Cyberhate using Scientometric analysis. The Scientometric study uses the Scopus database, including all the publications till 2023. The results identify major contributors, significant publications, prominent journals, core research areas, and emerging trends that guide future researchers to explore eminent topics.

articleTitle: Enterprise Security Architecture For Cloud Computing: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cloud computing has transformed IT in recent years by isolating application and data resources from foundational structures. Providing high-quality service, however, necessitates guaranteeing cloud computing security. Security risks develop when apps run outside of the defined firewall and into the public domain. Any security compromise in a cloud component might be catastrophic for both the organization (the client) and the supplier. As a result, we present in this study a framework and technique for cloud security that can detect cloud computing security concerns.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Federated Learning CNN for Interactive Virtual Tours of UNESCO Cultural Heritage Sites: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cultural heritage places play a significant role in our shared history and identity, and their survival needs to be preserved and promoted. A federated learning CNN model for interactive virtual tours of culturally significant locations is presented in this paper. Utilizing the Federated Averaging technique and the MoblieNet CNN architecture, we trained the model on a simulated federated learning environment with 20 devices. Ten thousand photographs from each of the four UNESCO World Heritage Sites—Angkor Wat, Stonehenge, Machu Picchu, and Petra—comprised the total 40,000 enhanced images used to train the model—a testing set of 4,000 photos with equal representation from each site. The model's parameter values ranged from 0.93 to 0.97, yielding % overall accuracy of 95.4%. The option to customize the tour based on individual interests and preferences, which was not possible in the centralized CNN model, was appreciated by the participants utilizing the federated learning CNN approach. The participants also well-liked the model's privacy and security features, increasing confidence in the system's operation. The findings of this research show that the federated learning CNN model is very accurate and precise for item recognition and categorization in cultural heritage locations. The model's personalized and secure user interface may improve the virtual tour experience and foster system trust.

articleTitle: Distributed data reduction with decision-making for IoT-based smart farming irrigation systems
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The more crucial process and one of the world's major consumers of water in agriculture is irrigation, which has been growing as a result of population growth and the resulting rise in demand for food. The irrigation system is one of the most important components of a system of agriculture. The crop's productivity will be directly influenced by the efficiency and applicability of the irrigation system. Water scarcity is one of the greatest challenges for an irrigation system. The efficient use of land, water, and energy resources depends on Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart agriculture systems. In this article, a distributed data reduction and decision-making (DiDaReD) approach for IoT-based smart farming irrigation systems is proposed. The DiDaReD approach is implemented on two levels: sensor devices and edge gateway. At the sensor device level, we implemented a lightweight scoring method for removing the redundant collected soil moisture readings before sending them to the edge gateway. At the edge of the gateway, a voting technique is applied to the scores of received readings from sensor devices to produce a decision regarding irrigation of the monitored farming field according to the soil moisture state of this field. Finally, since the DiDaReD approach is periodic and works in real-time, we implement a decision reduction algorithm to prevent sending the same decision notifications to the actuator, thus saving the energy of the IoT network. Several experiments are implemented using real sensed data from the farming field, and the conducted results show that the proposed DiDaReD outperforms other methods in terms of data reduction ratio, number of sent readings, energy consumption, network lifetime, data integrity, decisions, and total energy consumed by the edge-gateway node.

articleTitle: Comparative Model: Video Based Fire Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurate detection is essential for prompt reaction and fire mitigation since fires represent a serious hazard to people’s lives and property. A family of deep learning models known as Convolution Neural Network (CNN) has demonstrated excellent potential in computer vision applications, such as fire detection. The abstract illustrates how CNNs may be used to accurately detect fire in a variety of situations by learning discriminative characteristics from video frames. A comparative study has been done on Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and CNN. Additionally, it examines the training procedure, the significance of data augmentation, and the structural elements of a typical CNN-based fire detection system.

articleTitle: A Brief Survey of Energy-Efficient Task Scheduling Algorithms in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Research and development in cloud computing technology have become one of the primary focuses for academics and enterprises because of its immense popularity, higher utility, and ever-increasing demand. Scheduling cloud tasks in an energy-efficient manner is challenging and has become an important area of research too.
